title: Add arrow-cpp to Spack environment and rebuild container
description: Apache Arrow is not in the current Spack view at local/. Add arrow-cpp to spack.yaml and rebuild the winch/ddm container image on the native host (Spack is owned by a different user inside the container). Verify Arrow cmake config is available inside the container at local/lib/cmake/Arrow*. This is a prerequisite for building wire-cell-arrow.
notes:
FIX APPROACH (Spack 1.1.0, all CLI / Containerfile-friendly). Two root causes found: (1) gcc-runtime mismatch — make-view.sh used 'spack view symlink <bare specs>' which matches the GLOBAL store and grabbed a gcc-runtime@12 arrow, colliding with the view's gcc-runtime@15; (2) putting the COMPILER (gcc@15) in the env/view forces a gcc12-bootstrap subtree (gcc@15 link-deps like zstd/zlib are built by the bootstrap gcc@12), which duplicates the %gcc@15 app-stack copies and collides in the view ('two specs project to the same prefix: zstd ...'). unify:true and packages:all:require:%gcc@15 cannot fix (2): a compiler cannot build its own deps.

CORRECT RECIPE:
BUILD TIME (image, /devel not mounted) -- compiler NOT a root spec:
  spack env create wcph
  spack -e wcph config add concretizer:unify:true
  spack -e wcph config add "packages:all:require:'%gcc@15'"
  spack -e wcph add cmake wire-cell-toolkit phlex 'arrow +parquet +compute +dataset +filesystem'   # NO gcc@15 here
  spack -e wcph concretize -f
  spack -e wcph install --fail-fast
RUNTIME (container, /devel/ddm mounted) -- replaces make-view.sh:
  spack -e wcph env view enable /devel/ddm/local
  spack -e wcph env view regenerate
COMPILER (kept beside, not inside, the app view): gcc@15 stays installed in the store; expose via .envrc:
  export CC="$(spack -e wcph location -i gcc@15)/bin/gcc"
  export CXX="$(spack -e wcph location -i gcc@15)/bin/g++"
wire-cell-arrow CMakePresets.json reads these via $env{CC}/$env{CXX} (no view g++, no hard-coded store hash).

NOTES: package is 'arrow' not 'arrow-cpp'. Residual '%c=gcc@12.2.0' on gcc@15 and its build deps is expected/benign. Diagnose dup-view errors with 'spack -e wcph find <pkg>' (compiler shows in the group header). Rebuild with compiler removed in progress 2026-06-11.
close_reason: Arrow now in the view and verified end-to-end. The view is provided by symlinking local/ -> the env's image-built default view (/spack/var/spack/environments/wcph/.spack-env/view); make-view.sh updated. 'spack env view enable' fails at runtime (rmtree on spack-owned view -> EACCES) and 'spack view symlink' fails ('Unknown namespace: wirecell') — see memory spack-runtime-view-permission. Confirmed: local/lib/cmake/{Arrow,Parquet}, local/include/arrow present, libstdc++ -> gcc-runtime-15.2.0. wire-cell-arrow scaffold configures (finds Arrow+WireCell+Boost::json), builds, links, and ctest passes.

title: T3.2: Ionization IFunctionNode<IPrimaryVertexSet,ITrackSegmentSet> + TG4HitSegment mapping
description:
The `Ionization` node — `IFunctionNode<IPrimaryVertexSet, ITrackSegmentSet>` +
`IConfigurable` — in the edep/ package.

## Flow
1. Hold an `EDepSim::TrackingService` initialized (once) with the configured
   physics_list, gdml and macro, and the WCT->G4 primary generator factory
   (task T3.1) so the generator is built on the Geant4 thread.
2. Per input `IPrimaryVertexSet`: feed the generator, `service.simulate(ident)`,
   receive the `TG4Event`.
3. Convert `TG4Event.SegmentDetectors` (map<sd-name, vector<TG4HitSegment>>) to
   `Aux::SimpleTrackSegment` objects and emit one `Aux::SimpleTrackSegmentSet`.

## Field mapping (mirror the existing Arrow chain, verified)
Reference: edep-sim-phlex/Observables.cpp segment_rows + wire-cell-phlex-arrow
Convert.cpp + wire-cell-arrow ArrowTrackSegment.
- start()/stop()  <- seg.Start.{X,Y,Z}() / seg.Stop.{X,Y,Z}()   (WCT Point)
- start_time()/stop_time() <- seg.Start.T() / seg.Stop.T()
- energy()        <- seg.EnergyDeposit
- secondary()     <- seg.SecondaryDeposit   (scintillation energy partition)
- n_electrons()   <- quanta model: n_q = energy / 19.5 eV;
                     n_photons = n_q * secondary/energy; n_electrons = n_q - n_photons
- track_length()  <- seg.TrackLength
- id()            <- seg.PrimaryId
- pdg()           <- lookup PrimaryId in a TrackId->PDG map built from
                     TG4Event.Trajectories (traj.GetTrackId()->traj.GetPDGCode())

## Units
CLHEP (edep-sim) -> WCT.  Both use MeV=1; confirm/handle length (mm) and time
(ns) via the unit-convention decision (D1) at this boundary.

## Config (IConfigurable)
- physics_list, gdml, macro (passed to TrackingService::initialize)
- optional sensitive-detector name filter (which SegmentDetectors to include)
- ionization/quanta W-value if not hard-coded

## Factory + tests
- WIRECELL_FACTORY(Ionization, ... INode/IFunctionNode, IConfigurable)
- test: build a Simple IPrimaryVertexSet (single muon), run the node, assert
  non-zero segments; then feed the result to TrackSegmentSampler -> IDepoSet.

title: [epic] wire-cell-toolkit edep/: run edep-sim inside WCT via EDepSim::TrackingService
description:
## Vision

Run edep-sim's Geant4 tracking INSIDE the Wire-Cell Toolkit as native WCT
data-flow nodes, using the reusable `EDepSim::TrackingService` (epic ddm-2ha).
A new optional `edep/` sub-package holds the (team-gated) edep-sim dependency;
the shared WCT data model (IData interfaces + aux Simple impls) stays
dependency-light.

This is the in-process WCT-native counterpart to the existing Arrow-based chain
(edep-sim-phlex -> edep.observables -> wc.tracksegmentset -> ITrackSegment),
which stays as the reference for field mappings and schemas.

## Two phases

**Phase 1 — Ionization.**  A `IPrimaryVertexSet` of primaries is fed to
edep-sim; the resulting TG4HitSegments are converted to an `ITrackSegmentSet`
(the existing WCT interface) which flows into the existing
`WireCell::Gen::TrackSegmentSampler` (IFunctionNode<ITrackSegmentSet,IDepoSet>)
-> depos -> the rest of WCT sim.

**Phase 2 — ParticleTracking.**  Model the FULL TG4Event with a new `ISimTruth`
IData and constituents (primary vertices, the particle trajectory tree, hit
segments, photon hits).  A `ParticleTracking` node produces `ISimTruth`.

## New shared data model (iface + aux, no edep-sim dependency)

Phase 1 (initial, this epic's F1):
- `IPrimaryParticle`  — pdg, momentum, energy, id + Configuration metadata for
  the rarer G4 attrs (name, mass, charge, polarization, proper_time, weight).
- `IPrimaryVertex`    — position, time, particles + metadata (generator,
  reaction, cross_section, weight, probability, ...).
- `IPrimaryVertexSet` — ident + vertices + metadata.
- aux Simple impls of each.

The design deliberately balances edep-sim's simple TG4* types and Geant4's rich
G4* types: the common core is first-class; rarely-used parts live in a JsonCPP
`Configuration` (already a WCT dependency).

Phase 2 constituents: `ITrajectory`(+set/tree), `IPhotonHit`(+set), `ISimTruth`.

## edep/ package (holds the edep-sim dependency)

- WCT `IPrimaryVertexSet -> G4PrimaryVertex` generator (analog of edep-sim-phlex
  GenEventKine), installed via the TrackingService custom-generator factory so
  it is CONSTRUCTED ON the Geant4 thread (affinity).
- `Ionization` node: IFunctionNode<IPrimaryVertexSet, ITrackSegmentSet>.
- `ParticleTracking` node (phase 2): IFunctionNode<IPrimaryVertexSet, ISimTruth>.

## Policy note

Per WCT CLAUDE.md, a new external dependency is team-gated.  edep-sim is that
dependency and is confined to the single optional `edep/` plugin (the compliant
structure: a dependency belongs to the one plugin that needs it).  See the
decision issue.

title: Decision: unit convention for TG4PrimaryVertex -> G4 reverse conversion
description: TG4PrimaryVertex stores Position (TLorentzVector) + TG4PrimaryParticle Momentum in edep-sim/ROOT output units; G4PrimaryVertex/Particle expect CLHEP units. Pin the position/time and momentum/energy scale factors. Blocks T2.3 (PrimaryVertexGenerator).
close_reason: RESOLVED: edep-sim uses CLHEP/Geant4 internal units (io/EDepSimUnits.h: mm=ns=MeV=eplus=1, documented as matching internal Geant4 units). TG4PrimaryVertex.Position and TG4PrimaryParticle.Momentum are therefore already in the units G4PrimaryVertex/G4PrimaryParticle expect. PrimaryVertexGenerator copies the raw doubles with NO scaling.

title: Decision: per-event RNG reseed policy from event_id (reproducibility vs statistical independence)
description: SimulateRequest.event_id is said to also seed the RNG. edep-sim exposes /edep/random/randomSeed <int>. Reseeding every event gives reproducibility but naive per-event reseeding can hurt statistical independence. Decide the mechanism and whether reseed is default-on. Blocks the reseed step in T2.4.
close_reason: RESOLVED: reseed per event_id. Mechanism: G4Random::setTheSeed(seed) (same call used by EDepSim::UserRunAction::SetSeed / the /edep/random/randomSeed macro), applied in do_simulate before /run/beamOn 1. seed = abs((long)event_id), matching SetSeed's positivity handling.

title: T2.5: do_shutdown teardown discipline (geometry-store Clean on worker + leak run manager)
description:
`TrackingWorker::do_shutdown()` — port the hard-won teardown discipline from
`edep-sim-phlex Tracking::G4Worker::loop()` tail. This is the single most
important correctness item in the epic; getting it wrong crashes at process exit.

On the worker thread, after the run loop breaks:

1. `G4GeometryManager::GetInstance()->OpenGeometry();` — required first because
   the geometry is closed/optimized after `/run/initialize`.
2. `G4PhysicalVolumeStore::Clean(); G4LogicalVolumeStore::Clean();
   G4SolidStore::Clean();` — empty the GLOBAL geometry stores HERE, on the thread
   that BUILT the volumes, so their main-thread process-exit static destructors
   find nothing to tear down. Otherwise the main-thread static destructor deletes
   worker-built volumes cross-thread → crash in `~G4PVPlacement`/`GetRotation`.
3. **Deliberately LEAK** the G4 objects: `(void)run_manager.release();` (and the
   persistency + generator). `~G4RunManager` is separately crash-prone at
   teardown and the service lives for the whole process, so releasing is the
   correct trade.

Critically, `~TrackingWorker` must NOT delete these G4 objects — the pimpl
holder releases them here. Verify a clean exit under asan/valgrind (F4).
close_reason: Done: doShutdown teardown (OpenGeometry + 3x Clean on worker thread; release/leak runManager+persistency+generator; idempotent; ~Worker deletes no G4). Runtime (asan/valgrind clean exit) tracked in F4/T4.1.

title: T2.4: do_simulate (feed, optional reseed, beamOn 1, harvest TG4Event)
description:
`TrackingWorker::do_simulate(const SimulateRequest&) -> shared_ptr<TG4Event>`:

1. Optionally reseed the RNG from `req.event_id` — GATED on the RNG-policy
   decision (`/edep/random/randomSeed <int>` macro or
   `CLHEP::HepRandom::setTheSeed`). Do nothing until that decision lands.
2. `generator.feed(*req.primaries)`.
3. `G4UImanager::GetUIpointer()->ApplyCommand("/run/beamOn 1")`.
4. The persistency manager's `Store()` has filled `fEventSummary`; copy/move
   `GetEventSummary()` into a `std::make_shared<TG4Event>` and return it
   (fEventSummary is overwritten on the next event, so must be copied — as phlex
   copies).
close_reason: Done: doSimulate (G4Random::setTheSeed(abs(event_id)) per ddm-2ha.5, generator Feed, beamOn 1, copy GetEventSummary() into shared_ptr<TG4Event>, stamp EventId).

title: T2.3: EDepSim::PrimaryVertexGenerator (TG4PrimaryVertexContainer -> G4 primaries)
description:
`EDepSim::PrimaryVertexGenerator` — a `G4VPrimaryGenerator` (direct, not an
`EDepSim::PrimaryGenerator` composite, since the input already carries vertex
positions/times) that converts a `TG4PrimaryVertexContainer` into G4 primaries.
Analogous to phlex's `GenEventKine` + `append_primaries`, but consuming the
native edep-sim type instead of HepMC3.

- `feed(const TG4PrimaryVertexContainer&)` (or hold a
  `shared_ptr<const ...>`): stash the container to be tracked by the next
  `GeneratePrimaryVertex`.
- `GeneratePrimaryVertex(G4Event*)`: for each `TG4PrimaryVertex`, make a
  `G4PrimaryVertex` from its `Position` (TLorentzVector) and, for each
  `TG4PrimaryParticle`, a `G4PrimaryParticle(PDGCode, px, py, pz, E)` from
  `Momentum`. `TG4PrimaryParticle` carries only PDGCode + Momentum 4-vector
  (no charge/polarization).

DEPENDS on the unit-convention decision: what units does `TG4PrimaryVertex`
store position/time and momentum in (edep-sim/ROOT output convention) vs the
CLHEP units G4 expects? Nail this down before finalizing the scale factors.
close_reason: Done: src/EDepSimPrimaryVertexGenerator.hh/.cc (TG4->G4, NO scaling per ddm-2ha.6). Compiles with -DEDEPSIM_FORCE_PRIVATE_FIELDS (uses only public accessors).

title: T2.2: do_initialize (CreateRunManager, base PersistencyManager, gdml+defaults+macros+/edep/update)
description:
`TrackingWorker::do_initialize(const InitializeRequest&)` — replaces the CLI
setup in `app/edepSim.cc` and mirrors `edep-sim-phlex Tracking::G4Worker::initialize()`:

1. `run_manager.reset(EDepSim::CreateRunManager(req.physics_list))`.
2. Install a plain `EDepSim::PersistencyManager` (NOT the Root one): its `Store()`
   fills `fEventSummary` each event but writes no ROOT file and builds no TGeo.
   It registers itself as the G4 persistency singleton. In the current fork
   `GetEventSummary()` is inline in `EDepSimPersistencyManager.hh` (no
   `SummaryPersistency` subclass needed — unlike phlex, which subclassed to work
   around an undefined accessor).
3. Construct `EDepSim::PrimaryVertexGenerator` (see sibling task) and inject via
   `UserPrimaryGeneratorAction::AddGenerator` (borrow the action from the run
   manager; `GetUserPrimaryGeneratorAction()` is const → const_cast, as in phlex).
4. Apply, via `G4UImanager`, in order: `/edep/gdml/read <gdml>` (if set);
   `/edep/control edepsim-defaults 1.0`; user macro commands (one per line, skip
   blank/`#`); optionally `/edep/validateGeometry` when `req.validate_geometry`;
   then `/edep/update` (triggers `/run/initialize`).

Guard: throw if the action is missing. Set an `m_initialized` flag.
close_reason: Done: doInitialize (CreateRunManager, base PersistencyManager, gdml + edepsim-defaults + macros + validateGeometry + /edep/update). -fsyntax-only clean.

This is the fix over Tracking which only guards initialize -> a per-event beamOn throw currently terminates the process. Cheap ctor; ~Worker must not delete G4 (see T2.5). pimpl to hide G4 headers.
close_reason: Done: TrackingWorker::run() std::visit dispatch + per-request try/catch -> Reply.error (the terminate fix over Tracking). Teardown moved after the loop so it also covers channel-close. -fsyntax-only clean.

title: F4: Tests + docs (integration, exception, adopt-mode, teardown-clean)
description:
## Problem

Prove the pattern end-to-end and document it: correct results, correct exception
translation, and — most importantly — a clean teardown (no cross-thread G4
crash) under sanitizers.

## Approach

- Integration test: build a `TrackingService`, `initialize` with a small GDML +
  a single-muon setup, `simulate` a one-vertex `TG4PrimaryVertexContainer`,
  assert the returned `TG4Event` has primaries/trajectories/segments, then let
  the service destruct and confirm a clean exit under asan/valgrind.
- Negative tests: a bad GDML/init throws and is delivered to the caller (not the
  worker thread); a per-event throw is translated (no `std::terminate`).
- Adopt-mode: exercise the "donate main()'s thread" construction — no extra
  thread spawned, same code path.
- Docs: README/example (optionally an adopt-mode variant of `app/edepSim.cc`).

Lives under edep-sim `test/`/`validate/`.
close_reason: F4 complete: ctest/ suite (channel, error-translation, threaded sim, adopt) all PASSING via real cmake+ctest; docs written.

title: F3: TrackingService — thread-safe front end + ThreadFactory
description:
## Problem

Implement `EDepSim::TrackingService`: the thread-safe, re-entrant front end that
client code constructs. It wraps and manages the worker's dedicated thread and
exposes blocking + non-blocking calls. No restriction on which/how many threads
call it — the `TrackingChannel` serializes.

## Approach

- Owns a `TrackingChannel m_chan;` and a `std::thread m_thread;` (declared after
  the channel on purpose). Ctor launches the thread via an injected
  `ThreadFactory`; the thread body constructs the `TrackingWorker` locally and
  calls `worker.run(m_chan)` — so the worker is born and dies on that thread.
- `submit(Request, Completion)` — the primitive; returns once the worker accepts.
- `call(Request)` — blocking convenience over `submit` + `std::promise`;
  rethrows `reply.error`.
- Typed helpers: `initialize(physics_list, gdml, macros)`,
  `simulate(TG4PrimaryVertexContainer, id) -> TG4Event`, `apply_macros(...)`.
- `simulate_async(primaries, id, cb)` — non-blocking, for a TBB `async_node`
  body (must not block a TBB worker).
- Dtor: `submit(ShutdownRequest{}, nullptr)`, `m_chan.close()`, `join()`.

Tasks: Service class + lifecycle; ThreadFactory (default/pinned/adopt);
simulate_async.
close_reason: F3 complete: TrackingService + ThreadFactory (default/pinned/adopt) + async, -fsyntax-only clean.

title: F2: TrackingWorker — all-Geant4-on-one-thread + exception translation
description:
## Problem

Implement `EDepSim::TrackingWorker`: everything Geant4, living entirely on the
one dedicated thread — constructed there, every `beamOn` there, and destroyed
there. This is where the thread-affinity contract is actually honored.

## Approach

- `run(TrackingChannel&)` loop: `recv()`, `std::visit`-dispatch to
  `do_initialize`/`do_macros`/`do_simulate`/`do_shutdown`, then invoke
  `msg.done(reply)`. Wrap the dispatch in `try{…}catch(...){ reply.error =
  std::current_exception(); }` so a per-event failure is delivered as a reply
  rather than terminating the process (the concrete fix over `Tracking`, which
  only guards `initialize`).
- Ctor is cheap; G4 objects are NOT built in the ctor (they need
  `physics_list`/gdml from `InitializeRequest` and correct `/edep/update`
  ordering). `~Worker` must NOT delete G4 objects (see the shutdown task).
- G4 headers hidden behind a `struct Impl` (pimpl) so the worker header stays
  Geant4-free.

Split into tasks: message loop + exception translation; do_initialize;
PrimaryVertexGenerator (TG4->G4); do_simulate; do_shutdown teardown discipline.
close_reason: F2 complete: TrackingWorker + PrimaryVertexGenerator implemented, -fsyntax-only clean against real Geant4/ROOT/CLHEP. Live-G4 validation is F4.

title: F1: TrackingChannel + message/reply protocol (framework-agnostic)
description:
## Problem

Define the framework-agnostic request/reply protocol and the depth-1 rendezvous
channel that carry work between `TrackingService` (any thread) and
`TrackingWorker` (the one dedicated G4 thread). No Geant4 in this layer, so it
is unit-testable on its own.

## Approach

- `Request = std::variant<InitializeRequest, ApplyMacroRequest, SimulateRequest,
  ShutdownRequest>`.
  - `InitializeRequest{ std::string physics_list; std::string gdml;
    std::vector<std::string> macros; bool validate_geometry; }` — NOTE the
    sketch omitted `physics_list`; `EDepSim::CreateRunManager` requires it.
  - `SimulateRequest{ std::shared_ptr<const TG4PrimaryVertexContainer> primaries;
    unsigned long event_id; }`.
- `Reply{ ReplyValue value; std::exception_ptr error; }`, where
  `ReplyValue = std::variant<Empty, SimulateReply>` and
  `SimulateReply{ std::shared_ptr<TG4Event> event; }`.
- `Message{ Request request; std::function<void(Reply)> done; }` (`done` may be
  null for fire-and-forget).
- `EDepSim::TrackingChannel`: `std::optional<Message>` slot guarded by a
  `std::mutex` + `m_free`/`m_ready` CVs; `send()` (caller blocks until worker
  accepts), `recv()` (worker; `nullopt` == closed → stop looping), `close()`.

Files: `src/EDepSimTrackingMessages.hh`, `src/EDepSimTrackingChannel.hh/.cc`
(picked up automatically by `src/CMakeLists.txt` `file(GLOB *.cc)`). io lib
provides `TG4PrimaryVertexContainer`/`TG4Event`.
close_reason: F1 complete: messages + channel implemented, unit test passes.

title: [epic] edep-sim: thread-affine simulation Service/Worker lifecycle in the library
description:
## Vision

Factor the Geant4 thread-affinity lifecycle pattern — currently embedded in
`edep-sim-phlex`'s `Tracking` class — into **edep-sim proper** as a small,
framework-agnostic (no TBB / WCT / Phlex types) set of library classes. This
lets the pattern be reused to integrate edep-sim into the Wire-Cell Toolkit and
be back-ported into `edep-sim-phlex` (`ddm-4nd.11`).

## Why the pattern exists

Geant4's sequential `G4RunManager` is **thread-affine**: the navigator/world it
builds live in `G4ThreadLocal` state, and the global geometry stores are torn
down by main-thread static destructors at process exit. So *all* Geant4 work —
construction, every `beamOn`, AND destruction (emptying
`G4PhysicalVolumeStore`/`LogicalVolumeStore`/`SolidStore` on the building
thread) — must happen on one dedicated `std::thread`. Building on one thread and
running/destroying on another corrupts G4 and crashes (e.g. in
`~G4PVPlacement`/`GetRotation`).

## Shape (three classes + one generator, namespace `EDepSim`)

- **`EDepSim::TrackingChannel`** — a depth-1 request/reply rendezvous: a
  mutex-protected single message slot with two condition variables (free/ready)
  and a `close()`. A queue of depth 1; the worker is serial and a G4 event
  dwarfs the handoff.
- **`EDepSim::TrackingWorker`** — everything Geant4. Constructed and destroyed
  ON the dedicated thread. `run(channel)` loops, `std::visit`-dispatches request
  messages to `do_initialize` / `do_simulate` / `do_shutdown`, and — critically
  — **catches every exception and returns it as a reply** (`std::exception_ptr`),
  so a per-event failure never terminates the process.
- **`EDepSim::TrackingService`** — thread-safe, re-entrant front end owned by
  client code. Manages the worker's dedicated thread via a `ThreadFactory`
  (default `std::thread`, CPU-pinned, or "adopt" the caller's thread for
  gdb/valgrind/CLI). Offers blocking (`simulate`) and non-blocking
  (`simulate_async`, for TBB `async_node`) calls.
- **`EDepSim::PrimaryVertexGenerator`** — a `G4VPrimaryGenerator` that converts
  the per-event input `TG4PrimaryVertexContainer` (= `std::vector<TG4PrimaryVertex>`,
  from the io lib) into `G4PrimaryVertex`/`G4PrimaryParticle`, injected via
  `UserPrimaryGeneratorAction::AddGenerator`.

## Contract

- One-time `initialize(physics_list, gdml, macros)` → builds `G4RunManager` via
  `EDepSim::CreateRunManager`, installs a plain `EDepSim::PersistencyManager`
  (fills `fEventSummary`, no ROOT file, no TGeo), applies gdml + edepsim-defaults
  + user macros + `/edep/update`.
- Per-event `simulate(TG4PrimaryVertexContainer, event_id)` → `beamOn(1)` →
  returns `TG4Event` (harvested from `GetEventSummary()`).

## Improvements over `edep-sim-phlex::Tracking` (baseline)

1. Explicit `Channel` + `variant<Request>` messages vs hand-rolled
   `job_ready`/`result_ready`/`stop` booleans.
2. **Per-request exception translation** — `Tracking` only catches `initialize`;
   a throw inside a per-event `beamOn` is currently uncaught on the worker
   thread → `std::terminate`. Fixed here.
3. Injected `ThreadFactory` (default / CPU-pinned / adopt) vs always plain
   `std::thread`.
4. Native `TG4PrimaryVertexContainer` input (not HepMC3) and `TG4Event` output,
   with no framework dependencies.

Must preserve `Tracking`'s hard-won teardown discipline (geometry-store cleanup
on the worker thread + deliberate leak of the run manager).

## Downstream consumers (separate follow-on)

- Rewire `edep-sim-phlex::Tracking` (`ddm-4nd.11`) onto this library Service.
- Integrate edep-sim into Wire-Cell Toolkit via the Service.
close_reason: Epic complete: EDepSim::TrackingService/Worker/Channel + PrimaryVertexGenerator implemented in devel/edep-sim/src, ctest/ suite (4 tests) PASSING via the real cmake+ctest pipeline (libedepsim recompiled with the new files), docs in doc/TrackingService.md. Follow-ons (WCT integration, phlex Tracking back-port onto this Service) tracked under ddm-4nd.

title: Anti-fiducial-interaction HepMC source (fixed pool, deterministic draw)
description:
A Phlex source node providing ND-simulation **anti-fiducial**-interaction
HepMC3 GenEvents drawn, for efficiency, from a **fixed pool** rather than
simulated/read fresh per event:

- Pool preloaded into memory once via the hepmc-phlex pool-loader (ddm-j08.2's
  dev task) — HepMC3 has no random-access reader, so preload is required for
  O(1) draws.
- Draw index per phlex cell computed **deterministically** from the
  phlex-random CBRNG (ddm-j08.1's dev task): `index = f(cbrng(seed, cell_id))
  mod pool_size` — reproducible under concurrency, no shared mutable state.

Depends on both dev tasks landing first.

title: Fiducial-interaction HepMC source (serial)
description:
A Phlex source node providing ND-simulation **fiducial**-interaction HepMC3
GenEvents, delivered **serially** (one per phlex cell), via the hepmc-phlex
sequential file-source node (ddm-j08.2's dev task) reading a fiducial-
interaction file in event order. No pooling or random draw — output order
follows input file order. No dependency on phlex-random (fiducial delivery
is not randomized).

title: hepmc-phlex: add HepMC3 file-source node + pool-loader utility
description:
## Amended per research (ddm-j08 research task, closed)

Add to `hepmc-phlex`:

1. A sequential file-source **provider node** using `HepMC3::ReaderFactory`
   (auto-detects Ascii/AsciiHepMC2/Root/RootTree/HEPEVT/LHEF/gz — all
   already built in the Spack view, no new dependency), emitting one
   `GenEvent` per phlex cell in file order. Same node shape as the existing
   `GenEventGun`/`GenEventSequence` (`hepmc_phlex/`, `modules/`). This is
   what F3's fiducial (serial) source will drive.
2. A pool-loader utility: reads a bounded file fully into an in-memory
   `std::vector<HepMC3::GenEvent>` once at job start, exposing O(1) indexed
   lookup. HepMC3 readers have **no** random-access/seek-by-index API
   (only sequential `read_event()` + forward `skip(n)`), so pre-loading is
   the only efficient way to support indexed draws. This is what F3's
   anti-fiducial (pool-draw) source will index into via the phlex-random
   CBRNG.

Add package-local tests per the existing hepmc-phlex testing gap (ddm-azg)
rather than only exercising this through downstream smoke tests.

title: Implement phlex-random package: default CBRNG
description:
## Amended per research (ddm-j08 research task, closed)

Implement `phlex-random`:

- Header-only counter-based PRNG (CBRNG) core, e.g. Random123-style
  Philox4x32 or Threefry4x64 — pick ONE DUNE default engine so downstream
  packages stop each inventing their own. Keyed by
  `(global_seed, stream_id, counter)`; no shared mutable state.
- Do **not** wait on Phlex's resources API (ddm-999, still absent in
  v0.3.2). Expose the generator to algorithms via the *unfold + seed
  data-product* idiom already shown in the phlex-design docs
  (registration-interface.qmd's `generate_random` example): a `seed`/`key`
  data product in scope, consumed by an unfold node that emits N draws.
- Design the CBRNG core type so it can be wrapped by a first-class "PRNG
  resource" later, once ddm-999's resources API lands, without changing its
  public interface.
- DUNE should ship this as the default so per-package algorithms needing
  randomness (e.g. F3's anti-fiducial pool draw) share one reproducible
  mechanism instead of ad-hoc `std::mt19937` (cf. the existing pattern in
  `reference/phlex/test/form/generate_vector.cpp`, which is NOT reproducible
  under concurrency and should not be emulated).

Cross-ref: [[ddm-999]], [[ddm-4nd.8]].

title: [research] Survey HepMC3 file I/O + integration approach for hepmc-phlex
description:
## Task

Determine what HepMC file I/O exists (HepMC3 library capabilities) and how
best to add file-reading support to `hepmc-phlex`:

1. Inventory HepMC3's Reader/Writer classes actually available in the
   xerosere Spack build.
2. Check whether any support random access / seeking by event index (needed
   for an efficient "pool" source).
3. Record conclusions on the parent feature (ddm-j08.2) before closing.

## Findings

Recorded on parent [[ddm-j08.2]] (hepmc-phlex file I/O). Summary:

- `hepmc-phlex` currently has only `GenEventGun`/`GenEventSequence`
  (config/code-driven); no file reading.
- HepMC3 (already built in `extern/envs/gcc15/view`, with rootIO + search
  companions) ships `ReaderAscii`, `ReaderAsciiHepMC2`, `ReaderRoot`,
  `ReaderRootTree`, `ReaderHEPEVT`, `ReaderLHEF`, `ReaderGZ`, and
  `ReaderFactory` (auto-detecting format) — no new dependency needed.
- No HepMC3 reader supports random access / seek-by-index: the `Reader`
  interface is sequential `read_event()` + forward `skip(n)` only.
  `ReaderMT<T,N>` is parallel *sequential* prefetch, not indexed access.
- Recommendation: add (a) a `ReaderFactory`-based sequential file source
  node (serves the fiducial/serial case), and (b) a pool-loader that reads a
  bounded file fully into an in-memory `vector<GenEvent>` once, exposing
  O(1) indexed lookup (serves the anti-fiducial pool-draw case) since
  HepMC3 itself cannot do that access pattern natively.

Full detail in [[ddm-j08.2]].
close_reason: Research complete; conclusions folded into ddm-j08.2 (feature) and ddm-j08.2.2 (dev task). HepMC3 (already built in the Spack view) provides full Ascii/Root/RootTree/HEPEVT/LHEF/gz reader/writer support via ReaderFactory, no new dependency needed; no HepMC3 reader supports random access/seek-by-index, so the anti-fiducial pool source needs a preload-into-memory + indexed-lookup design rather than repeated file reads.

title: [research] Survey Phlex PRNG support: design doc + current code
description:
## Task

Determine how Phlex handles (or intends to handle) pseudo-random numbers:

1. Check current `reference/phlex` code for any PRNG facility (resource,
   utility, or ad-hoc pattern).
2. Check `reference/phlex-design` for design intent (conceptual +
   technical-design chapters, requirements).
3. Evaluate JAX-style counter-based/stateless generators as the model DUNE's
   `phlex-random` package should follow.
4. Record conclusions on the parent feature (ddm-j08.1) before closing.

## Findings

Recorded on parent [[ddm-j08.1]] (Phlex PRNG support). Summary:

- Current phlex v0.3.2 has no PRNG facility and no resources API at all
  (consistent with [[ddm-999]]/ddm-4nd.8, re-confirmed here). Only ad-hoc
  `std::mt19937` in a test fixture (`test/form/generate_vector.cpp`).
- `phlex-design`'s `resources.rst` "Random Number Resource" section commits
  to counter-based RNGs (CBRNGs) for concurrent reproducibility (DUNE req
  36) — the same family JAX's stateless/splittable PRNGKey design uses. But
  `ch_technical_design/random_numbers.rst` is an empty stub: no design
  written yet, and it's gated on the (unimplemented) resources API.
- A resources-API-free path already exists in the design docs: an *unfold*
  node consuming a `seed` data product (registration-interface.qmd:214-245),
  giving reproducibility via data-product provenance instead of a shared
  resource. This is directly compatible with a CBRNG keyed by
  `(global_seed, stream_id, counter)`.
- Recommendation: build `phlex-random` now on the unfold/seed-data-product
  idiom, independent of ddm-999, with a CBRNG core that can later be
  wrapped as a first-class resource once ddm-999 lands.

Full detail in [[ddm-j08.1]].
close_reason: Research complete; conclusions folded into ddm-j08.1 (feature) and ddm-j08.1.2 (dev task). Current phlex v0.3.2 has no PRNG facility and no resources API (confirms ddm-999/ddm-4nd.8); design docs commit to CBRNGs (JAX-style) but the technical-design chapter is an empty stub; a resources-API-free unfold+seed-data-product path already exists in the design docs and is what phlex-random should use now.

title: ND random-HepMC GenEvent source package (fiducial + anti-fiducial)
description:
## Problem

Provide a Phlex source of "random" HepMC3 GenEvent interactions for ND
(near-detector) simulation assumptions:

- one source delivers **fiducial** interactions, serially;
- a second source delivers **anti-fiducial** interactions, which for
  efficiency are drawn from a **fixed pool** in a deterministic
  pseudo-random manner (not re-simulated/re-read per event).

Depends on F1 (`phlex-random` CBRNG) for the deterministic draw and F2
(`hepmc-phlex` file I/O) for reading the underlying event files/pools; do
not start implementation until both land.

title: hepmc-phlex: HepMC3 file I/O support
description:
## Problem

`hepmc-phlex` (devel/hepmc-phlex) currently only produces events from
in-code/config-driven sources (`GenEventGun`, `GenEventSequence`) — there is
no way to read `HepMC3::GenEvent`s from a file. Determine what HepMC3 file
I/O is available and how it should be wired into hepmc-phlex.

## RESEARCH CONCLUSIONS (2026-08-25, see closed research task)

- `hepmc-phlex` today: `hepmc_phlex/{GenEventGun,GenEventSequence}.{hpp,cpp}`
  + `modules/{gen_event_gun,gen_event_sequence}.cpp`, both Phlex **source
  (provider)** nodes. No file reading anywhere in the package.
- HepMC3 is already in the Spack view
  (`extern/envs/gcc15/view`, libHepMC3.so.4 + libHepMC3rootIO +
  libHepMC3search) with a **full I/O layer already built**, at
  `extern/envs/gcc15/view/include/HepMC3/{Reader,Writer}*.h`:
  `ReaderAscii`, `ReaderAsciiHepMC2` (legacy), `ReaderRoot`/`ReaderRootTree`
  (ROOT-backed), `ReaderHEPEVT`, `ReaderLHEF`, `ReaderGZ` (gzip wrapper), and
  `ReaderFactory` (`deduce_reader`, auto-detects format from file content).
  So adding file I/O to hepmc-phlex needs **no new external dependency**.
- `ReaderMT<T,N>` is **not** random access — it's N sequential readers each
  pre-skipped by a fixed offset to prefetch ahead of one caller. The HepMC3
  `Reader` interface only exposes sequential `read_event()` + forward
  `skip(n)`; there is no seek-by-event-index API anywhere in the library.
- **Implication for the planned anti-fiducial "pool" source (see F3):**
  because HepMC3 readers can't cheaply seek to an arbitrary index, the
  efficient design is to read a bounded pool file **once, fully, into an
  in-memory `std::vector<HepMC3::GenEvent>`** at job start (a plain
  sequential read loop with any Reader), then do O(1) indexed lookups keyed
  by the phlex-random CBRNG draw — not repeated file I/O per draw.

## Recommendation

Add two things to hepmc-phlex:
1. A sequential file-source node using `HepMC3::ReaderFactory` (format
   auto-detected: Ascii/Root/RootTree/HEPEVT/LHEF/gz all "just work"),
   producing one `GenEvent` per phlex cell — same provider-node shape as
   `GenEventGun`/`GenEventSequence`. This directly serves F3's fiducial
   (serial) source.
2. A pool-loader utility: read a file fully into an in-memory
   `vector<GenEvent>` once, expose indexed lookup. This serves F3's
   anti-fiducial (pool-draw) source.

title: Phlex PRNG support: phlex-random package
description:
## Problem

Phlex's pseudo-random-number story is unclear: is there a current mechanism,
does the design intend one, and should DUNE provide its own default (a
`phlex-random` package)? Investigate JAX-style counter-based/stateless
generators as the likely model, since Phlex's own design docs point the
same direction.

## RESEARCH CONCLUSIONS (2026-08-25, see closed research task)

- **Current phlex (v0.3.2, `reference/phlex`) has no PRNG facility at all.**
  No CBRNG, no framework "resource" API of any kind (`grep resource
  phlex/**/*.hpp` only turns up `resource_usage` CPU/mem telemetry — this
  matches the existing ddm-999/ddm-4nd.8 finding that the resources
  registration API (`m.resource<>()`/`handle->make<>()`) from the design docs
  is simply not implemented yet, re-confirmed here against v0.3.2). The only
  extant random-number code in the phlex tree is `test/form/generate_vector.cpp`:
  a plain `std::mt19937` held as node instance state, seeded from config or
  wall-clock time — not reproducible across concurrent scheduling, no
  thread-safety contract, and not meant to be a general facility.
- **The design intent is explicit and matches JAX's approach.**
  `reference/phlex-design/doc/ch_conceptual_design/resources.rst` has a
  "Random Number Resource" section: DUNE requires reproducible random
  numbers under concurrency (`:need:DUNE 36`, spelled out in
  `doc/appendices/requirements.rst:196-204`), and instead of the usual
  stateful-engine-plus-locking workaround, Phlex intends to support
  **counter-based random number generators (CBRNGs)** specifically for
  this. CBRNGs (Random123's Threefry/Philox family) are exactly the
  primitive underlying JAX's stateless/splittable `PRNGKey` design:
  `output = f(key, counter)` with no shared mutable state, so any thread/
  partition/event can compute its stream independently and reproducibly.
- **But the technical-design chapter is an empty stub.**
  `doc/ch_technical_design/random_numbers.rst` is title-only — the CBRNG
  design hasn't been written up, and it is gated on the general resources
  API (tracked by ddm-999), which has no ETA.
- **A resource-free path already exists in the design docs.** 
  `registration-interface.qmd:214-245` shows an *unfold* node example
  (`generate_random`) that takes a `seed` **data product** (not a resource)
  and produces N random values as an output sequence — reproducibility via
  data-product provenance/threading, no shared state, no resources API
  needed. This composes naturally with a counter-based generator: derive a
  stream from `(global_seed, stream_id, counter)`.

## Recommendation

Don't wait on ddm-999 (resources API). Ship a small `phlex-random` package
now:
- Header-only CBRNG core (e.g. Random123-style Philox4x32 or Threefry4x64 —
  pick ONE DUNE default so packages stop inventing their own), keyed by
  `(global_seed, stream_id, counter)`.
- Expose it to algorithms today via the existing unfold + seed-data-product
  idiom (no dependency on phlex resources).
- Design the core type so it can be wrapped by a first-class "PRNG resource"
  later, once ddm-999 lands, without changing its public interface.

Cross-ref: [[ddm-999]] (resources API gate), [[ddm-4nd.8]] (prior resources-API
confirmation against v0.3.0).

title: [epic] ND random-HepMC event sourcing: phlex-random PRNG + hepmc-phlex file I/O
description:
## Problem

DUNE ND (near-detector) simulation needs a Phlex source of "random" HepMC3
GenEvent interactions: fiducial interactions delivered serially, and
anti-fiducial interactions drawn (for efficiency) from a fixed pool in a
deterministic pseudo-random manner. Building that source package first
requires two supporting pieces that don't yet exist:

1. A Phlex-side pseudo-random-number facility (design intent vs. current
   capability, then a `phlex-random` package DUNE can default to).
2. HepMC3 file I/O support in `hepmc-phlex` (currently config/code-driven
   sources only: `GenEventGun`, `GenEventSequence`).

## Scope

- F1 — Phlex PRNG support (`phlex-random` package)
- F2 — `hepmc-phlex` HepMC3 file I/O
- F3 — ND random-HepMC-GenEvent source package (fiducial + anti-fiducial),
  gated on F1 and F2

Each of F1/F2 carries a research task first; conclusions get folded back
into the feature and into F3's dev tasks before implementation starts.

title: F1.3 Core: block-sparse tensor (Block/SGrid/chunkify/accumulate) from tred
description:
Port tred's Block-Sparse-Binned representation to C++ libtorch: a `Block`
(batched equal-shape boxes with integer `location`/`shape`/`data`), a super-
grid `SGrid` (envelope/align), `chunkify` (re-tile to fixed chunk shape), and
`accumulate` (scatter-add of overlapping chunks via unique+index_add). This is
the memory/compute-efficient carrier exploiting ionization sparsity + response
locality. Source: `reference/tred/src/tred/{blocking,sparse,chunking}.py`.

title: F1.1 Core: drift transport + absorption(+fluctuation) + diffusion (batched depos)
description:
Core drift physics on batched depo tensors: transport to the response/anode
plane, absorption `1-exp(-dt/lifetime)` with optional binomial fluctuation,
and diffusion width growth `sigma = sqrt(2*D*dt + sigma0^2)` added in
quadrature (longitudinal + transverse), plus timing/`toffset` and the
bulk/near "drift vs anti-drift" region handling. Mirror `gen/src/Drifter.cxx`
and `reference/tred/src/tred/drift.py` (`transport`/`absorb`/`diffuse`); do NOT
reproduce the `DepoTimeCompare` self-compare bug. Config-free API.

title: F0.4 Core-vs-glue source layout + libspng-prep policy
description:
Decide the core-vs-glue source layout inside `spng/` (directory/naming
convention separating config-free torch core from WCT `INode` glue) so the
core can later be lifted into `libspng.so` with minimal churn. Document the
"relax the separation + file a libspng follow-up" policy for unavoidable WCT
coupling. This task seeds the companion libspng epic.

title: F0.3 Geometry-at-the-boundary contract (AnodePlane/Pimpos/wire-schema -> compact per-plane params)
description:
Specify the geometry-at-the-boundary contract: a single boundary component
that converts `IAnodePlane`/`Pimpos`/wire-schema into compact per-plane
parameters (pitch magnitude/direction/origin, impact count, wire/channel count
and ordering, per-plane baseline, plane-X) plus the response tensor handle, so
the core carries only dense arrays with no wire objects. Define what the core
is allowed to know vs what stays outside. Reference `gen/` usage audit
(`Pimpos`, `Response::as_array` row=impact/col=tick).

title: F0.2 Sim tensor data model: dense per-plane arrays + depo/segment layouts + datapath schema
description:
Define the sim tensor data model on top of TDM: the dense per-plane array
conventions (implicit row/column meaning, e.g. impact/wire row x tick column),
the depo-tensor and line-segment-tensor layouts (cf. tred depo schema
(c1..cN,w1..wN,ne) and step schema (b,e,w,ne)), and the `datatype`/`datapath`/
`parent`/`batches`/`derived_from` metadata schema for each sim product. Decide
naming and provenance conventions. Output: a `spng/docs/*.org` spec + the
`make_*`-style helper API sketch.

title: F0.1 Blessed vs verboten SPNG node inventory (reference doc)
description:
Produce a durable inventory (doc + Beads note) classifying every relevant
`spng/` node/class as BLESSED (reuse/example) or VERBOTEN (ignore), with the
evidence (base class, creation date, datapath vs tag idiom). Seed content is in
the epic description. Include the ambiguous cases (`TdmDecon` WIP stub,
re-created `FrameToTorchSet`). This is the reference every later task consults.

title: F1 Core libtorch sim library (config-free primitives)
description:
Implement the config-free *core* libtorch library: mid-level functions and
classes over `torch::Tensor`/plain data with no dependence on other WCT code,
no config parsing, and no `WireCell::Configuration`. These are the reusable
building blocks the thin TDM nodes (F2) will wrap. Reuse existing SPNG core
(`Convo.h`, `DFT.h`, `TorchLMN.h`, `Util.h`) wherever possible.

title: F0 Foundations: sim TDM data model, node inventory, geometry-boundary, layout policy
description:
Establish the shared foundations for the simng node family before core/node
code is written: the sim tensor data model, the blessed/verboten node
inventory, the geometry-at-the-boundary contract, and the core-vs-glue source
layout policy that prepares the future libspng extraction.

title: simng: vectorized libtorch (SPNG/TDM) simulation nodes
description:
Add a new family of **libtorch-vectorized detector-simulation nodes to
`spng/`** that reimplement the conceptual algorithms currently provided by
WCT's `gen/` subpackage (drift, noise generation, depo-transform /
response convolution, and digitization) using SPNG's newer "TDM" (Tensor
Data Model) node strategy, and that map in the desirable extensions
prototyped in the Python/PyTorch `tred` package.

## Motivation

- `gen/` implements the physics correctly but is CPU/scalar, monolithic
  (nodes "do too much"), and entangled with per-wire/per-channel geometry.
- `spng/` already provides a mature, vectorized, CPU/GPU libtorch
  processing stack for *signal processing*, but has **no torch/TDM
  simulation nodes**. Today `spng/cfg/spng/sim.jsonnet` merely wires the OG
  `gen/` nodes (`DepoSetDrifter`+`Drifter`, `DepoTransform`, `AddNoise`,
  `Digitizer`, `DepoFluxSplat`) operating on `IDepo`/`IFrame`.
- `reference/tred/` demonstrates a clean PyTorch reimplementation with
  valuable extensions (3D response, block-sparse tensors, line-segment
  ionization + Gaussian quadrature, dynamic per-layer batching) we want in
  C++.

## Note on "sim/" -> "gen/"

The WCT simulation code lives in `devel/wire-cell-toolkit/gen/`, not `sim/`.
The best design references are the April-2026 examination docs under
`gen/docs/examination/` (drifting-and-transport, noise-modeling,
response-and-convolution, diffusion-and-deposition,
digitization-and-pipeline, wire-and-anode-geometry) plus `gen/docs/noise.org`
and `gen/docs/depofluxsplat.org`.

## Design tenets

1. **Two source categories.** *Core* code = mid-level functions/classes over
   libtorch whose API is in terms of `torch::Tensor`/plain data, with **no**
   dependence on other WCT code, no config-file parsing, and no
   `WireCell::Configuration`. *Node* code = thin WCT `INode` implementations
   (SPNG TDM base classes) that only marshal config <-> tensor I/O. This
   prepares the future extraction of a standalone `libspng.so` (see the
   companion libspng epic). Where strict separation would cause substantial
   duplication/awkwardness, relax it and file a follow-up under the libspng
   epic rather than contorting the core.
2. **More, smaller nodes.** Follow SPNG's lead: prefer many nodes each with a
   small context (e.g. one node processes a single wire plane) over
   `gen/`-style loops over three planes.
3. **Geometry to the periphery.** Erase individual wires/channels and their
   spatial arrangement from the core; carry data as dense arrays whose
   rows/columns have an *implicit* meaning (e.g. impact/wire row x tick
   column). Convert `AnodePlane`/`Pimpos`/wire-schema into compact per-plane
   parameters exactly once, at the subgraph boundary.
4. **Reuse blessed SPNG.** Build on the newer TDM stack and reuse existing
   ops instead of re-deriving them (see reuse/ignore lists below).

## Reuse (blessed) vs ignore (verboten)

BLESSED — reuse or use as example (post-2025-09 TDM stack):
- Data model: `ITorchTensor`, `ITorchTensorSet`, `SimpleTorchTensor(Set)`,
  `TensorDataModel.h` helpers (`datapath`, `datatype`, `parent`, `batches`,
  frame/traces/chids/summaries/chmasks).
- Node bases: `TorchFunctionNode` (= `FunctionNode`+`ContextBase`; semaphore
  + no-autograd guard + inputs-on-device), `FunctionNode`, `TensorFilter`,
  `TensorSetFilter`, `FaninBase`/`FanoutBase`, `ContextBase`, `Logger`,
  `HanaConfigurable`.
- Core torch (already config-free): `Convo.h` (`linear_shape`, `convo_spec`,
  `filtered_decon_2d`), `DFT.h` (`FasterDftSize`), `TorchLMN.h` (LMN
  resample), `Util.h` (`gaussian1d`, padding helpers), `TensorTools.h`.
- Ops/spectra: `SPNGKernelConvolve` (the convolution engine),
  `SPNGResponseKernel` (FR(x)ER `ITorchSpectrum` that already carries the
  ADC-count `scale = gain*(1<<res)/(fullscale[1]-fullscale[0])`),
  `SPNGResampler`, `SPNGRebaseliner`, `SPNGRebinner`, `SPNGTransform`.
- Boundary interop: `SPNGFrameToTdm`, `SPNGTdmToFrame`, `SPNGTdmToTensorSet`.

VERBOTEN — ignore (2025-08-19 first-generation nodes): `SPNGDecon`
(`Decon.cxx`), `SPNGApply1DSpectrum`, `TorchTensorSet{Replicator,Collator,
Stacker,Unstacker,Tagger}`, `SPNGApplyROI`, OG MP-coincidence, `SPNGDNNROI`
(superseded by `SPNGDNNROI{Pre,,Post}Process`), `SPNGThresholdROIs`,
`Torch1DSpectrum`, `TorchFRERSpectrum`, `FrameToTorch`/`TorchToTensor`/
`TorchPacker`/`TorchSetUnpacker`. AMBIGUOUS: `TdmDecon.h` is a WIP stub with
no `.cxx` and no factory — do not build on it.

## Mapping tred features into simng

- Thin `nn.Module` "layers" with math in free functions -> SPNG TDM nodes
  (glue) + config-free core functions. tred layer order Drifter -> Raster ->
  ChunkSum -> LacedConvo -> readout maps to our drift -> charge/raster ->
  accumulate -> convolve -> noise -> digitize node chain.
- Block-Sparse-Binned tensor (`tred/blocking.py::Block`, `sparse.py::SGrid`,
  `chunkify`, `chunking.accumulate` scatter-add) -> a C++ block-sparse
  representation exploiting ionization sparsity + response locality.
- 3D detector response (`tred/response.py::ndlarsim`, `quadrant_copy`) in
  addition to WCT's 2D per-plane response.
- Line-segment ionization + Gauss-Legendre quadrature (`tred/raster/steps.py`
  `qline_diff3D`, `create_wu_block`, `eval_qeff`, `compute_qeff`) alongside
  point depos.
- Dynamic per-layer batching (`tred/plots/graph_effq.py` `batch_scheme` +
  `iter_chunk_block`/`iter_tensor_chunks` narrow views + `concat_blocks` +
  `accumulate`) with peak-memory tracking.

## Feature breakdown

- F0 Foundations: sim TDM data model, blessed/verboten inventory,
  geometry-at-the-boundary, core/glue layout policy.
- F1 Core libtorch sim library (config-free primitives).
- F2 SPNG TDM sim nodes (thin glue), per-plane.
- F3 Dynamic batching / rebatching between sim layers.
- F4 Jsonnet config + subgraph assembly + detector integration.
- F5 Validation, parity vs `gen/`, and tests.

## Non-goals

- Not deleting or refactoring `gen/`; simng is additive.
- Not the actual `libspng.so` extraction (companion epic) — only preparing
  the seam.
- Recombination/ionization models and kinematics upstream of depos are out of
  scope (depos/segments are the input).

title: wire-cell-phlex: imaging island module (IFrame → vector<IBlobSet> collect shape)
description:
Add the WCT imaging ISLAND module to devel/wire-cell-phlex: consumes one IFrame,
runs a WCT imaging sub-graph, and emits the whole stream of IBlobSet (one per
time slice) as a SINGLE Phlex product wrapping std::vector<IBlobSet::pointer>.

## The boundary-crossing problem

The imaging graph (…BlobSetSync) emits a STREAM of IBlobSet, one per slice.
FunctionExecutor<In,Out> (ShapeExecutors.hpp) drains exactly ONE output per
input, so it cannot carry the whole stream. BoundarySink already QUEUES every
output; we need a shape that drains the ENTIRE queue into one product.

## Pieces to add (all in devel/wire-cell-phlex)

1. Data.hpp: a wrapper for the collected product. There is no WCT IData for
   "vector of IBlobSet", so add e.g.
     struct BlobSets { std::vector<WireCell::IBlobSet::pointer> items; };
   (and optionally `using BlobSet = Data<WireCell::IBlobSet>` for the item).
   Include <WireCellIface/IBlobSet.h>.

2. ShapeExecutors.hpp: port_traits<WireCell::IBlobSet> with sink_iface =
   ISinkNode<IBlobSet>, snk_class = "BlobSetBoundarySink", stem = "blobset".
   (source side not required for a collect shape.)

3. BoundaryNodes.cpp: WIRECELL_FACTORY(BlobSetBoundarySink,
     wcphlex::BoundarySink<WireCell::ISinkNode<WireCell::IBlobSet>>,
     WireCell::ISinkNode<WireCell::IBlobSet>, WireCell::IConfigurable)
   + the IBlobSet include.

4. A new "collect" executor shape (e.g. CollectExecutor<In, Item>) in
   ShapeExecutors.hpp: fills the In (IFrame) boundary source, run_graph(), then
   DRAINS the Item (IBlobSet) sink in a loop until drain() returns nullptr,
   packing all into a BlobSets wrapper. It reuses PortedExecutor plumbing for
   the single input source + single sink but overrides the drain to collect all.
   (Simplest: give BoundarySink a drain-all or loop drain() in the executor.)

5. register_shapes.hpp: register_collect<In, Item>() helper producing node name
   "wcph_<in>_to_<item>s" (e.g. wcph_frame_to_blobsets) via m.transform, reading
   the same inputs/outputs config arrays convention (1 input selector, 1 output
   suffix).

6. modules/frame_to_blobsets.cpp (or frame_to_blobs.cpp): one-line body calling
   wcphlex::register_collect<WireCell::IFrame, WireCell::IBlobSet>(m, config).
   Add to the module CMake list (mirror deposet_to_frame). Verify resulting
   library name matches run.sh's plugin-path expectations.

## Notes

- The WCT sub-graph is provided by the imaging Jsonnet (separate task) and wired
  via the injected sources/sinks TLAs exactly like sim-sigproc.jsonnet.
- Follow the module naming/registration convention documented in
  register_shapes.hpp and deposet_to_frame.cpp.

title: wire-cell-arrow: wc.blobs schema + write-side converter (+ unit test)
description:
Add the "wc.blobs" Apache Arrow schema + write-side converter to
devel/wire-cell-arrow (namespace WireCell::Arrow), the package that owns all
wc.* schema builders (wire_cell_arrow/Converters.{hpp,cpp}).

## What to add

The product is a VECTOR of IBlobSet (elements span time slices). Encode it as
one flat table, ONE ROW PER IBlob:

- blobset_index : int32   (index of the IBlobSet in the vector)
- slice_ident   : int32   (ISlice::ident(); common to all blobs in the set)
- slice_start   : float64 (ISlice::start())
- blobset_ident : int32   (IBlobSet::ident())
- blob_ident    : int32   (IBlob::ident())
- value         : float32 (IBlob::value())
- uncertainty   : float32 (IBlob::uncertainty())
- face_ident    : int32   (IBlob::face()->ident())
- strips : list<struct<layer:int32, lo:int32, hi:int32>>
      from RayGrid::Blob::strips(): each Strip = {layer, bounds.first,
      bounds.second} (half-open ray bounds). INCLUDE all 5 layers (the 2
      special horizontal/vertical bound layers + U,V,W).
- corners: list<struct<layer1:int32, ray1:int32, layer2:int32, ray2:int32>>
      from RayGrid::Blob::corners(): each crossing_t = pair<coordinate_t,
      coordinate_t>, coordinate_t = {layer, grid}. (grid == ray index.)

Column names follow the wc.* convention (e.g. "wc.blob.value",
"wc.blobs.blobset_index" — pick the naming to match the existing
tracksegment/depo columns).

## API surface (match tracksegmentset)

- blob_schema() / blobs_schema(int ident) builders using the shared
  semantic_metadata() stamper (schema name "wc.blobs", the set ident carried in
  schema metadata "wc.blobs.ident" — NOT a column), so wire-cell-phlex-arrow can
  re-stamp a foreign table's metadata (see Convert.cpp:170-179 precedent).
- arrow::Result<std::shared_ptr<arrow::Table>> to_arrow(
      const WireCell::IBlobSet::vector& blobsets)   // or a suitable pointer-vector type
  filling columns row-by-row. The nested list<struct> columns follow the
  wc.depo.priors list<struct> builder pattern (Converters.cpp:117-150,185-244):
  ListBuilder wrapping a StructBuilder.

## Types (already confirmed)

- WireCellIface/IBlobSet.h: ident():int, slice():ISlice::pointer, blobs():
  IBlob::vector, shapes():RayGrid::blobs_t.
- WireCellIface/IBlob.h: ident():int, value():float, uncertainty():float,
  face():IAnodeFace::pointer, slice():ISlice::pointer, shape():const RayGrid::Blob&.
- WireCellIface/ISlice.h: ident():int, start():double.
- WireCellIface/IAnodeFace.h: ident():int.
- WireCellUtil/RayTiling.h: Strip{layer_index_t layer; grid_range_t bounds;},
  Blob::strips()->const strips_t&, corners()->const crossings_t&.
- WireCellUtil/RayGrid.h: layer_index_t=int, grid_index_t=int,
  coordinate_t{layer,grid}, crossing_t=pair<coordinate_t,coordinate_t>.

## Build + test

- Add schema/converter code into Converters.{hpp,cpp} (append to add_library
  source list in CMakeLists.txt only if new .cpp files are created).
- New test/test_blobset_converter.cpp modeled on test_tracksegment_converter.cpp:
  build a concrete SimpleBlobSet/SimpleBlob (check devel/wire-cell-toolkit/aux/
  inc/WireCellAux/ for Simple* helpers; if none exist, construct minimal blobs
  via RayGrid::Blob::add), to_arrow(), table->ValidateFull(), assert schema +
  column values, plus empty-set case. Register in test/CMakeLists.txt with
  ${WIRECELL_RUNTIME_LIBS}. Package builds -Wall -Wpedantic -Werror, C++23.

## Deferred

Read-side facade (ArrowBlobSet reconstructing IBlobSet from a table) is a
separate lower-priority task; the workflow only needs the write side.

title: [epic] WCT 3D imaging (tiling) as a Phlex workflow → wc.blobs Arrow schema
description:
Add WCT "3D imaging" (tiling) as a Phlex workflow, downstream of signal
processing in the SPDIR chain (extends epic ddm-179).

## Goal

Run WCT 3D imaging (time-slicing + grid tiling) inside Phlex so that an IFrame
produced by signal processing (and, separately, by DepoFluxSplat "true" signal)
is turned into blobs, recorded to Apache Arrow under a new "wc.blobs" schema,
and persisted to the SPDIR HDF5 output. Verify and visualize via python/wct-
metrics.

## Imaging workflow (per anode, 3-view to start)

Input IFrame (from SP or splat) ->
  MaskSlices (time slicing)        -> stream of ISlice
  -> SliceFanout (mult 2)          -> one ISlice per anode face
  -> 2x GridTiling (face 0, face 1)-> one IBlobSet per face per slice
  -> BlobSetSync (mult 2)          -> one merged IBlobSet per slice

Reference config: devel/wire-cell-toolkit/cfg/pgrapher/experiment/pdhd/img.jsonnet
(img.slicing + img.tiling; we stop after tiling, no solving/clustering yet).

As with the other wire-cell-phlex configs, the imaging Jsonnet is detector-
independent and takes a detector-specific object for PDHD and PDVD (via
cfg/dune/wct/dets.jsonnet). Start with a 3-view tiling (active_planes=[0,1,2]);
the multi-2view/dead-channel variants are deferred.

## Boundary-crossing design (the crux)

The WCT imaging graph emits a STREAM of IBlobSet (one per time slice). The
existing FunctionExecutor<In,Out> shape drains exactly one output per input, so
it does not fit. The imaging island needs a NEW executor shape that runs the WCT
graph on one input IFrame and COLLECTS the whole IBlobSet stream (already queued
by BoundarySink) into a single Phlex product wrapping a std::vector<IBlobSet::
pointer>. This "collect" shape + an IBlobSet BoundarySink + a vector-carrying
wrapper type are new pieces in devel/wire-cell-phlex.

## "wc.blobs" Arrow schema

New schema representing the vector of IBlobSet spanning time slices. Records,
per IBlob: the IBlobSet vector index, ISlice::ident() and ISlice::start()
(common to all blobs in a set), IBlobSet::ident(), IBlob::ident()/value()/
uncertainty(), the owning IAnodeFace::ident(), the RayGrid::Blob shape as its 5
strips (layer + half-open [lo,hi) ray bounds, incl. the 2 special bounds
layers), and the Blob corners() crossings (each = a pair of ray-grid coordinates
(layer,ray)). Only indices are stored, not physical points. Lives in wire-cell-
arrow (schema/converter) + wire-cell-phlex-arrow (TableGroup bridge + convert
dispatch).

## Command / tests

Extend tests/spdir/run.sh with TWO imaging sub-graphs: one fed by the SP
(a_simsp) frame, one by the splat (a_splat) "true" frame; keep the two outputs
DISTINCT and save both to the SPDIR HDF5. Add tests for the intermediate parts
and final verification + visualization in python/wct-metrics (iterated/expanded
after the workflow runs well enough for reasonable initial output).

## Scope (initial)

- 3-view tiling only (PDHD + PDVD); dead-channel multi-2view/active variants
  deferred.
- Stop after tiling (no BlobClustering/ChargeSolving/clustering yet).
- No physical-point mapping in the schema (indices only).

title: Phlex node main-thread initialize() hook (fixes concurrent go-jsonnet cgo crash)
description:
## Problem (concrete)

The split full-chain smoke tests abort under default parallelism with a Go
runtime crash:

```
fatal error: traceback did not unwind completely
...
github.com/google/go-jsonnet.(*interpreter).manifestJSON(...)
main.jsonnet_evaluate_file(...)
_cgoexp_..._jsonnet_evaluate_file(...)
```

Reproduce (this repo):

- `devel/wire-cell-phlex-arrow/test/run-fullchain-split.sh` — aborts (default `-j 64`)
- `devel/wire-cell-phlex-arrow/test/run-fullchain-split-depos.sh` — passes ONLY
  because it runs `phlex -j 1` as a workaround.

### Root cause

Each WCT "island" is a Phlex node backed by a templated shape executor
(`devel/wire-cell-phlex/modules/register_shapes.hpp` →
`FunctionExecutor`/`SinkExecutor`/`SourceExecutor`). On first invocation an
executor evaluates its `wct_config` Jsonnet via the embedded **go-jsonnet**
engine through a **cgo** entrypoint (`jsonnet_evaluate_file`). Phlex invokes
node bodies on TBB worker threads, so with >1 worker two islands can enter the
go-jsonnet cgo call concurrently (or on a non-main thread). The Go runtime's
scheduler/stack handling is not compatible with being driven that way from
foreign threads, and it aborts.

`-j 1` serializes node bodies onto effectively one context and avoids it, but
that defeats Phlex's concurrency and only masks the real gap.

## The general problem

This is one instance of a broader missing capability, under active discussion
upstream:

  https://github.com/orgs/Framework-R-D/discussions/764

Phlex has a **node construction** phase (main thread, during registration /
`framework_graph::finalize()`) and a **node execution** phase (TBB worker
threads). There is **no post-construction, pre-execution entry point that runs
on the main thread**. Many real algorithms need exactly that: one-time setup
that must happen once, before any concurrent execution, and/or on the main
thread — e.g. driving a non-thread-safe library, warming a cache, opening a
handle, or (here) invoking a cgo/go-jsonnet evaluation that must not run
concurrently on worker threads.

Today the only workarounds are: do the setup lazily inside the node body (racy;
needs its own locking; still runs on a worker thread — which is exactly what
breaks go-jsonnet), or serialize the whole job (`-j 1`).

## Ask

Design a minimal, backward-compatible way for Phlex to call a node's
`void initialize()` (when the node type provides one) exactly once, on the main
thread, after all nodes are constructed and before graph execution begins. Bare
functions and classes that do NOT provide `initialize()` must remain valid node
implementations with zero behavior change. Detection via a template/concept.

The deliverable is a concrete proposal (below, in the issue's design notes) to
communicate to the Phlex developers — grounded in phlex v0.3.2 source — showing
that the feature slots into the existing lifecycle without disturbing the
current design.

## Acceptance

- A written design against phlex v0.3.2 identifying (a) the type-erasure
  boundary where a typed node object is still available, (b) a
  detection trait/concept for `initialize()`, (c) the main-thread
  post-construction/pre-execution invocation point, and (d) the backward-compat
  argument for bare functions/lambdas/classes without `initialize()`.
- Once available upstream, the wire-cell-phlex shape executors move their
  Jsonnet evaluation into `initialize()` and the split smoke tests pass at
  default parallelism (drop the `-j 1` workaround).
design:
# Proposal: opt-in main-thread `initialize()` for Phlex nodes

Grounded in **phlex v0.3.2** (`reference/phlex`, tag v0.3.2, commit 29b8b3a).

Goal: if a node's underlying algorithm type provides `void initialize()`, Phlex
calls it exactly once, on the main thread, after all nodes are constructed and
before graph execution begins. Otherwise nothing changes.

## Where the typed object still exists (detection site)

Phlex erases the user's algorithm into a `std::function` very early, in
`phlex/metaprogramming/delegate.hpp`. `algorithm_bits<Bound, Algorithm>`
receives the concrete bound object and immediately erases it:

```cpp
// delegate.hpp  (v0.3.2)
template <typename Bound, typename Algorithm>
class algorithm_bits {
  using bound_type = Bound;                 // = std::function<...>
  template <typename T>
  algorithm_bits(T object, Algorithm algorithm)      // T = std::shared_ptr<U>
    : bound_{delegate(std::move(object), std::move(algorithm))} {}
  auto release_algorithm() { return std::move(bound_); }
  Bound bound_;
};
```

The three `delegate()` overloads show the two categories that must both stay
legal:

- **bare function / lambda** → `delegate(std::shared_ptr<void_tag>, ...)`; the
  bound object is `void_tag` — there is no instance, so no `initialize()`.
- **class method node** (`g.make<MyClass>().transform(&MyClass::op, ...)`) →
  `delegate(std::shared_ptr<T>, R (T::*)(Args...))`; here a real `T` instance
  exists and MAY define `initialize()`.

So `algorithm_bits`'s constructor is the single point where a typed
`std::shared_ptr<U>` is in hand before erasure. That is where we detect and
capture.

## (a) Detection trait

```cpp
// delegate.hpp
template <typename U>
concept has_initialize = requires(U& u) { u.initialize(); };
```

Detection is on `U`, the element type of the bound object's `shared_ptr`. For
`U = void_tag` (bare functions/lambdas) the concept is false, so those nodes are
unaffected — this is the backward-compatibility guarantee, enforced by the type
system, not by convention.

## (b) Capture the initializer alongside the algorithm

Have `algorithm_bits` build a `std::function<void()>` init thunk that shares
ownership of the same object (copy the `shared_ptr` before it is moved into
`delegate`). Empty thunk == "no initializer".

```cpp
// delegate.hpp — helpers
inline std::function<void()> make_initializer(std::shared_ptr<void_tag> const&) {
  return {};                                   // bare function / lambda: no-op
}
template <typename U>
std::function<void()> make_initializer(std::shared_ptr<U> const& obj) {
  if constexpr (has_initialize<U>)
    return [obj] { obj->initialize(); };        // shares ownership; runs later
  else
    return {};                                  // class without initialize(): no-op
}

// algorithm_bits: add one member + one accessor; init it BEFORE bound_.
std::function<void()> initializer_;
template <typename T>
algorithm_bits(T object, Algorithm algorithm)
  : initializer_{make_initializer(object)},     // copies shared_ptr
    bound_{delegate(std::move(object), std::move(algorithm))} {}
auto release_initializer() { return std::move(initializer_); }
```

(Declare `initializer_` before `bound_` so it is constructed while `object` is
still intact; `make_initializer` takes it by const-ref and only copies the
shared_ptr.)

## (c) Carry the thunk to the node, run it on the main thread

The node object is the right owner: it is exactly the set of things the
framework already tracks, and only successfully-registered nodes get one.

`AlgorithmBits alg` already flows into every node constructor, where the body is
extracted via `alg.release_algorithm()` (see `declared_transform.hpp:84`,
`declared_observer.hpp:68`, `declared_predicate.hpp:72`, `declared_fold.hpp:97`,
and the provider path `registration_api.hpp:146`). At each of those sites also
pull `alg.release_initializer()` and store it.

The consumer family (transform / observer / predicate / fold / unfold / output)
shares the base `products_consumer` (`products_consumer.hpp:20`), and the
framework already enumerates them via `node_catalog::consumers()`
(`node_catalog.hpp:34`). Add there:

```cpp
// products_consumer (base)
void set_initializer(std::function<void()> f) { initializer_ = std::move(f); }
void initialize() { if (initializer_) initializer_(); }   // called once, main thread
std::function<void()> initializer_;
```

`provider_node` (`provider_node.hpp:20`) and `source` (`source.hpp`) are the two
node kinds outside that base; give each the same two-line addition and a catalog
accessor (or a tiny shared mix-in if preferred). These are the node types
`register_source` / sources produce, which the WCT shape executors use, so they
must be covered too.

Invoke on the main thread between construction and execution — a new step in
`framework_graph::execute()`, which itself runs on the caller's (main) thread:

```cpp
// framework_graph.cpp
void framework_graph::execute() {
  ...
  finalize();          // main thread: builds all edges (existing)
  initialize_nodes();  // NEW, main thread: run each node's initializer once
  run();               // activates source; dispatches to TBB workers (existing)
}

void framework_graph::initialize_nodes() {
  for (auto* c : nodes_.consumers())            c->initialize();
  for (auto& p : nodes_.providers | std::views::values) p->initialize();
  for (auto& s : nodes_.sources   | std::views::values) s->initialize();
}
```

Ordering note: initializers run sequentially in an unspecified order, before any
worker task. If cross-node init ordering ever matters that is a separate
feature; the one-time, main-thread, pre-execution guarantee is what solves the
cases in #764 and the go-jsonnet crash.

## (d) Backward compatibility

- Bare functions and lambdas: bound object is `void_tag`, `has_initialize` is
  false, `make_initializer` returns an empty thunk, `initialize()` is a no-op.
  No source change required for any existing node.
- Class nodes without `initialize()`: `has_initialize<U>` false → same no-op.
- Class nodes WITH `initialize()`: opt in simply by defining the method; no new
  registration syntax, no macro, no base class to inherit.
- Everything is resolved at compile time; the only runtime cost is one
  `if (initializer_)` per node at startup.

## Why this fits Phlex's current design

- No new public registration API; opt-in is "define `void initialize()`".
- The detection lives exactly at the existing erasure boundary
  (`algorithm_bits`); nothing upstream of it needs the concrete type.
- The invocation point is a natural sibling of the existing `finalize()` step in
  `execute()`, on the same (main) thread, using structures the framework already
  holds (`node_catalog`).
- Total surface: `delegate.hpp` (trait + thunk + one member/accessor),
  `products_consumer` + `provider_node` + `source` (two lines + accessor each),
  the node constructors (one line each to pull the thunk), and one new
  `framework_graph` step.

## Downstream payoff (this repo)

`devel/wire-cell-phlex/modules/register_shapes.hpp` builds
`FunctionExecutor`/`SinkExecutor`/`SourceExecutor` as `std::shared_ptr` captured
in a lambda. Refactor so the executor is the node object (a class method node)
and move its one-time `wct_config` Jsonnet evaluation (the go-jsonnet cgo call)
into `executor->initialize()`. It then runs once, on the main thread, before any
TBB worker — eliminating the concurrent-cgo crash and letting the split smoke
tests run at full `-j`.
acceptance_criteria: Written design vs phlex v0.3.2 covering: (a) type-erasure boundary with a typed node object (algorithm_bits/delegate.hpp), (b) initialize() detection concept, (c) main-thread post-construction/pre-execution invocation point (framework_graph::execute between finalize and run), (d) backward compat for bare functions/lambdas/classes without initialize(). Follow-up: wire-cell-phlex shape executors move Jsonnet eval into initialize(); split smoke tests pass at default -j (drop -j 1 workaround).

title: WCT gen: TrackSegmentSampler (config-selected ionization function object -> IDepoSet)
description:
Per the ADR decision: the sampler is a WCT component in gen/ on branch
'track-segment-sampling' -- class Gen::TrackSegmentSampler implementing
ITrackSegmentSampler (+ IConfigurable), consuming ITrackSegmentSet, emitting
IDepoSet of Aux::SimpleDepo.

Scope:
- IONIZATION MODES via stored function object (ADR point 3): configure() reads a
  mode/model config parameter and stores a std::function (or equivalent) member
  computing N_e per segment; operator() has NO per-call mode if():
  - quanta: N_e from the segment's n_electrons (upstream 19.5 eV split;
    no re-fluctuation).
  - recombination (default): dE/dx = energy/track_length; delegate to the existing
    Gen::{Birks,Box,Mip}Recombination via IRecombinationModel (named component,
    configured with efield/density from WCT Jsonnet -- consistent with how the
    models are already consumed in gen/).
- SAMPLING (accepted ADR point 4): uniform along start->stop at config step_size
  (cf. Gen::TrackDepos), positions+times linearly interpolated, N_e apportioned
  conserving the segment total; zero-length segment -> one point depo;
  deterministic in v1.
- Depo fields: charge = electron count with the WCT sign convention (resolve +
  test-assert: recombination models return negative via Wi=23.6eV/(-eplus);
  TrackDepos negates; confirm Drifter/DepoTransform expectation), energy MeV,
  id/pdg from the segment, extents 0 (Drifter adds diffusion), prior nullptr.
- Config surface (WCT Jsonnet): mode, recombination model type/name, efield,
  density, Wi override, step_size.
- WCT component registration (WIRECELL_FACTORY) so Jsonnet can name it.

Exercisers:
- gen/test unit tests on synthetic SimpleTrackSegmentSets: charge conservation,
  endpoint/timing interpolation, step-size edge cases.
- PHYSICS ACCEPTANCE: MIP segment (dE/dx ~ 2.1 MeV/cm) at 500 V/cm ->
  recombination factor ~0.7, ~6-7e4 electrons/cm (anchor numbers in
  gen/test/test_recombinationmodels.cxx, kGeVToElectrons=4.237e7).
- A tiny WCT-only job (wire-cell CLI jsonnet): synthetic segment source ->
  TrackSegmentSampler -> DepoSetDumper/sink, runnable without Phlex.
acceptance_criteria: Gen::TrackSegmentSampler builds + registers on the branch; unit + physics-acceptance ctests pass; standalone wire-cell jsonnet job produces sensible depos in both modes; charge sign documented and asserted.
notes:
=== IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-30, Claude) on wire-cell-toolkit branch track-segment-sampling ===
Commit 13aa9e8: gen/WireCellGen/TrackSegmentSampler.{h,cxx} implementing
ITrackSegmentSampler + IConfigurable (Aux::Logger; WIRECELL_FACTORY with INamed).
Per the ADR: configure() selects the ionization model ONCE into a std::function
member -- no per-call if().  Modes: 'recombination' (default; named
IRecombinationModel component via Factory::find_tn, default BoxRecombination;
Efield/rho/Wi configured on THAT component per WCT norms) and 'quanta'
(producer n_electrons; negative=unknown -> ValueError; no re-fluctuation).
Sampling: N=max(1,ceil(|stop-start|/step_size)) depos at sub-interval centers,
linear time interpolation, exact charge+energy conservation, id/pdg carried,
extents 0, EOS passthrough, SimpleDepoSet keeps input ident.  Depo charge is
NEGATIVE electrons (Drifter: 'Electrons should be negative').

CRITICAL PHYSICS FIX (commit e6fb7e f): Gen::Birks/BoxRecombination had a 10x
units bug -- spurious *units::cm on the dE/dX factor inflated the quenching
term, giving R~0.31 instead of ~0.70 for a MIP at 500 V/cm (dE() inverses too).
test_recombinationmodels.cxx only PRINTS, asserts nothing, so it never caught
this.  Fixed + now asserted by the new doctest (R in [0.6,0.8], ~6.3e4 e/cm,
inverse round-trip).  BEHAVIOR CHANGE for existing Birks/Box users (clus dQ/dx)
-- UPSTREAM PROMPTLY.  gen doctests 7/7, clus 49/49 green after fix.

Deviation from acceptance: the standalone WCT-only jsonnet job is NOT included
-- it needs an ITrackSegmentSet source/sink pair which does not exist yet; the
doctest exercises the component through the factory exactly as a job would, and
the in-graph exercise arrives with the ddm-69y.5 mini job (tracksegmentset ->
sampler -> deposet sink).  WCT installed to the shared prefix; build cache
restored to WCT_WITH_TESTS=OFF.
close_reason: Gen::TrackSegmentSampler implemented with function-object mode dispatch; doctests green incl. MIP physics anchors; required fixing a 10x units bug in Gen::Birks/BoxRecombination (flagged for upstreaming). Standalone jsonnet job deferred to the ddm-69y.5 mini job (needs source/sink pair).

title: ADR: segment-sampler design + package factoring (input/output types, ionization modes, truth keys)
description:
Ratify the segment-sampler design before implementation. Research is done (2026-07-30
session); this issue records the proposal and Brett's decision. This is the
sampler-specific instance of the general factoring decision ddm-4nd.10.

## Proposed decisions

1. INPUT = the Q5 canonical edep.observables TableGroup (member 'segments', schema
   edep.segments), NOT the native TG4Event. Rationale: Arrow lingua franca; keeps
   Geant4/ROOT/HepMC3 out of the sampler; Q5 (ddm-4nd.5) already designated a separate
   downstream segments->wc.deposet node. Cost: edep.segments drops per-segment pdg
   (only primary_id + contributors survive) -> additive schema-v2 column (child issue).

2. OUTPUT = wcphlex::DepoSet (wire-cell-phlex Data.hpp:54; SimpleDepoSet of
   WireCell::Aux::SimpleDepo). Drops straight into wcph_deposet_to_frame. Persistence
   for free via existing wire-cell-phlex-arrow to_table_group(DepoSet) -> wc.deposet.
   IDepo mapping: charge = ionization-electron count (VERIFY sign convention: WCT
   recombination models emit negative via Wi=23.6eV/(-eplus); TrackDepos negates too;
   confirm what Drifter/DepoTransform expect), energy = MeV, id = primary_id (see 5),
   pdg = from schema v2 (0 until then), extents = 0 (Drifter adds diffusion),
   time/pos interpolated along the segment. Units already aligned (CLHEP mm/ns/MeV
   == WCT units).

3. IONIZATION = strategy object with two config-selectable modes:
   - quanta: N_e = n_electrons column as-is (19.5 eV quanta model, upstream
     SecondaryDeposit split; NO re-fluctuation). Physically gated by ddm-496.
   - recombination (proposed DEFAULT until ddm-496 resolves): N_e via WCT
     Gen::BirksRecombination / BoxRecombination / MipRecombination from
     energy_deposit, dE/dx = energy_deposit/track_length, E-field + density from
     config (E-field sourced from the detector object; schema gains 'efield').

4. SAMPLING = uniform along the Start->Stop line (per TG4HitSegment.h: energy is
   deposited uniformly), config step_size (a la Gen::TrackDepos), N_e split across
   samples conserving total charge; deterministic (no added fluctuation) in v1.
   Note TrackLength (incl. delta-rays) may exceed |stop-start|; use straight-line
