title: BlobDepoFill: give depos Morse-measured SP-broadening smear before filling blob charge (currently diffusion-only, isotropic transverse)
description:
## Problem

BlobDepoFill (img/src/BlobDepoFill.cxx) fills "true" charge onto blobs formed
by tiling a signal-processed (SP) frame. Those blob boundaries are broadened
relative to the raw depo distribution by two effects baked into the SP chain:
filter response broadening, and mismatch between the per-wire-region *average*
detector response used by SP/simulation vs the *detailed* per-wire response of
the simulation/real detector. This extra broadening is measured empirically
per detector via the "Morse" procedure and is fed into DepoFluxSplat's
"true"-signal frame as `det.splat.smear_long`/`smear_tran` (3-element
[U,V,W]-plane arrays, see e.g. dune/wct/dets/pdhd/detector.jsonnet `splat:`
block) — see gen/src/DepoFluxSplat.cxx:310-336, which quadrature-adds
`smear_long[iplane]` (converted length via `* tick * speed`) into the
per-depo longitudinal sigma, and `smear_tran[iplane]` (converted to length via
`* wire pitch`) into the per-depo transverse sigma, independently *per wire
plane* before diffusing/binning the depo onto that plane's traces.

BlobDepoFill instead works directly from the *raw drifted depos* with none of
this extra smearing:

- img/src/BlobDepoFill.cxx:121-124 (slice_and_dice_depos): `tsigma =
  idepo->extent_long()/speed` — pure diffusion, no `smear_long` term.
- img/src/BlobDepoFill.cxx:143 (same function): `wsigma =
  idepo->extent_tran()` — pure diffusion, no `smear_tran` term, and applied
  only along the single "primary" plane's pitch axis (`m_pindex`, config
  `pindex`, default the collection plane) via `pimpos.transform(...)`. The
  other two planes get no explicit smearing role at all in BlobDepoFill.

Net effect: blobs are correctly *shaped* (tiled from the SP frame, which does
carry the smear), but the "true" charge BlobDepoFill assigns them is
distributed using a narrower, purely-diffusive, isotropic-transverse depo
than the one that produced those blob boundaries. This is a systematic
mismatch between blob shape and the charge distribution used to fill it.

## Why this isn't a simple one-line fix

`IDepo::extent_tran()` (iface/inc/WireCellIface/IDepo.h:45-48) is a single
scalar: "Any (half width) extent in the transverse (pitch) direction... The
distribution is implicit... (e.g. Gaussian)". It models the transverse spread
as circularly symmetric in the plane perpendicular to drift. That's
sufficient for DepoFluxSplat because DepoFluxSplat treats each wire plane
independently: it projects the depo onto plane P's own pitch axis and adds
that plane's own `smear_tran[P]` in quadrature — three independent 1D
projections, never combined into one consistent 2D/3D shape.

BlobDepoFill instead needs one *consistent* charge distribution because it
integrates the SAME depo against wire strips from multiple planes at once (it
already assembles per-blob bounds from all views — see the `strips`/`irel`
loop at BlobDepoFill.cxx:326-358 — to constrain the wire range on the primary
plane). Per Brett: the physically correct picture is that the depo, projected
into the transverse (anode) plane, is NOT circularly symmetric once you add
Morse smearing: the collection-plane (Z, e.g. W) smearing maps directly onto
smearing along the Z axis, while the two induction planes' smearing (U, V) —
each measured along its own tilted pitch direction — must be recombined
(with cosine-angle terms from each plane's wire angle relative to Z/Y) to
recover the smearing along the anode's other axis (Y). The result is an
elliptical (three-unique-widths-worst-case, since long/tran differ too)
transverse depo shape, not a single scalar sigma.

## Suggested direction (per Brett, not mandated — open to design)

Apply the extra 3D smearing internally within an upgraded BlobDepoFill,
rather than trying to push a non-circular shape through the existing
`IDepo::extent_tran()` scalar (which other consumers, e.g. DepoFluxSplat,
GaussianDiffusion-based sim, rely on staying a simple isotropic scalar).
Concretely:
- Take the same per-plane `smear_long`/`smear_tran` (already detector-config
  data, `det.splat.smear_long/smear_tran`) as new BlobDepoFill config.
  Long-axis smearing already reduces cleanly to one number since drift
  direction is common to all planes (mirrors DepoFluxSplat's `sigma_L`
  handling).
- Derive the transverse ellipse (e.g. width along Y and Z, or a full 2x2
  covariance) by combining `smear_tran[U]`, `smear_tran[V]`,
  `smear_tran[W]=Z` through each plane's wire angle, replacing the current
  single `idepo->extent_tran()`-derived `wsigma` in `slice_and_dice_depos()`.
  W(collection)'s smear maps directly to Z; U/V require the cosine-angle
  recombination described above to recover the Y-component.
- `slice_and_dice_depos()` currently dices only along the primary plane's
  pitch (BlobDepoFill.cxx:138-158); check whether other planes' wire-range
  intersections (via the `strips`/`irel` bounds loop) also implicitly assume
  isotropic transverse spread and would need the elliptical shape too, or
  whether they only use the blob's static shape bounds (already fixed by
  tiling) and are unaffected.

## Where to verify

tests/spdir (xerosere, epic ddm-3bu) is a convenient harness: it already
produces both the SP-tiled blobs (img_sp) and DepoFluxSplat-tiled/BlobDepoFill
-filled blobs (img_splat) with the *same* smear_long/smear_tran-aware "true"
frame vs a currently-unsmeared BlobDepoFill fill, so before/after charge
distributions can be compared directly (e.g. via python/wct-metrics blobs, or
Bee export tests/spdir/run-bee.sh) once this is implemented.

title: PDVD SP-frame imaging yields 0 blobs (splat works)
description: In spdir (osp, pdvd) the SP-imaging tap (img_sp: SumSlices charge>0 over OSP gauss ROIs -> BlobClustering -> BlobSolving) produces 0 blobs, while img_splat (SumSlices over splat frame -> BlobDepoFill) produces ~1234. Both use the same anode/img.jsonnet, so the tiling geometry works. The SP gauss frame has traces (~2412/event). Investigate: gauss trace tag vs img_sp sum_tag='gauss'; per-plane presence of gauss signal (3-view coincidence); PDVD-specific OSP output structure. Parent epic ddm-3bu.

comments.author: Brett Viren
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE found. PDVD SP-imaging yields 0 blobs because OmnibusSigProc produces NO collection-plane (W) output; without the 3rd view the ray-grid tiling finds no blobs (splat works because it isn't OSP-gated).

Evidence chain (spdir osp pdvd, event0; PDVD anode0 channel map: U 0-475, V 952-1427, W 1904-2487):
- SP frame has traces only on channels <=1394 (U+V, both faces); ZERO on W (1904-2487), for gauss AND wiener tags.
- Independent of FR file: tried protodunevd_FR_norminal_260324 (colleague's), _3view_speed1d55, and _imbalance3p_260501 (dunereco's own) -- all fail W identically.
- FR collection responses are present + normal-sign (unipolar negative) but WEAK: norminal W central trough -0.000598 vs dune-garfield-1d565 W -0.004364 (~7x weaker), and weaker than PDVD's own induction (U -0.000723).
- Sim ADC tap (pre-OSP) confirms the sim DOES produce collection signal but WEAK: W max |ADC-baseline| ~175 vs induction ~414; noise peak ~40-50. So collection SNR is marginal.
- DECISIVE: lowering troi_col_th_factor 5.0 -> 2.0 recovers W (0 -> 819 W traces, chan range now 31-2482) and imaging (img_sp 0 -> 27 blobs).

=> The weak PDVD collection field response makes the collection ADC signal fall below the 5-sigma troi_col ROI threshold, so no collection ROIs form. Fix is a physics/tuning decision (like the narrow-Wiener): (a) lower troi_col_th_factor for PDVD, and/or (b) renormalize/replace the collection field response so collection > induction as expected. NOT applied pending expert input. Note img_sp=27 << splat ~1234 at troi_col=2.0, so a threshold tweak alone is a marginal recovery -- the response normalization is the more likely real fix.

comments.author: Brett Viren
comments.text:
REFINED root cause via new tests/fr-path-sums.py + shape analysis:

FR IS CORRECTLY NORMALIZED: fr-path-sums.py integrates each FR path over time; the
collection-plane collecting paths integrate to ~1.0 for ALL PDVD FRs (norminal 1.0000,
imbalance3p 1.0000, 3view 1.0000) exactly like dune-garfield-1d565 (1.02). So the W
response is NOT under-normalized in charge. (Script captured under xerosere/tests/, general
tool: collecting paths ~1.0, neighbours ~0.0, O(1%) domain error expected.)

The W response is BROAD in time, not low in charge: collection central-path width(>10% peak)
= 2400 ns for PDVD-norminal vs 300 ns for dune (~8x broader); peak 0.0006 vs 0.0044 (~7x
lower). Same integral spread over ~8x the time => ~8x lower peak. A broad collection response
deconvolves to a weak, spread-out gauss that falls below the 5-sigma troi_col threshold =>
no collection ROIs => no 3-view tiling => 0 blobs. (Lowering troi_col 5.0->2.0 recovers it
weakly, confirming amplitude-below-threshold.)

RULED OUT: filter zero-frequency suppression. hf_filter flag=true zeroes only the DC bin;
flipping it on the time filters (Gaus_tight+Wiener_tight_W flag:false) AND on the wire filter
(Wire_col flag:true) each left W absent (0 collection traces). Elec response cancels between
sim and SP (same component), so not elec.

=> The problem is the PDVD collection FIELD-RESPONSE TIME SHAPE (8x too broad). This is an
FR-file property (Garfield calc / drift-speed-time-scaling), NOT normalization/filters/elec.
Next: FR-generation review (expert), or accept + lower PDVD troi_col as a tuning workaround.

comments.author: Brett Viren
comments.text:
ELEC top/bottom reconciliation (expert raised elec):

Our PDVD config ALREADY splits electronics by anode: anodes 0-3 (bottom drift) use
ColdElecResponse (gain 7.8 mV/fC, shaping 2.2us -- same width/type as PDHD/PDSP), anodes 4-7
(top drift) use JsonElecResponse dunevd-coldbox-elecresp-top-psnorm_400.json.bz2. Confirmed
the top Json elec IS very broad (~17900 ns / 18us wide vs ColdElec 2.2us). So the top-elec
point is real and correctly handled -- it will matter for anodes 4-7.

BUT our spdir/imaging test runs anode_index=0 = BOTTOM = the sharp ColdElec. So anode0's weak
collection is NOT a broad-elec problem; it already uses the correct sharp bottom elec.

response_plane=18.1cm matches dunereco (18.1cm) and the FR origin (181mm) -- no mismatch.

The collection weakness on the BOTTOM anode traces to the collection FIELD response, which is
collection-SPECIFICALLY broad (best-path 5%-extent): PDVD W=2000ns vs dune W=800ns (~2.5x),
peak ~0.001 vs 0.0039 (~3.6x lower). Induction is NORMAL width (PDVD U/V 7300/7500ns vs dune
7400/4900ns), so it is NOT a global drift-speed/time-scale bug -- it is specific to the
collection plane, and identical across all 3 PDVD FR files (norminal/imbalance3p/3view).

Net: elec is correctly configured for bottom; the residual bottom-anode collection weakness
is driven by the collection field-response time-shape. Open question for FR authors: is the
~2.5x broader / ~3.6x lower-peak PDVD collection field response expected physics, or an FR
collection-plane generation issue? Tool tests/fr-path-sums.py confirms charge normalization
(integral=1.0) is fine.

comments.author: Brett Viren
comments.text:
FR width + PDF analysis (tests/fr-path-sums.py, now with widths + --pdf). Ran on dune-1d565 (PDSP/PDHD generic), np04hd-6paths-mcmc-bestfit + np04hd-6paths (PDHD APA0), and the 3 PDVD FRs. Collection-plane wire-0 integral / width:
  dune-1d565           -0.986 / 400 ns   (WORKS)
  np04hd-mcmc-bestfit  -0.999 / 400 ns   (collection is at planeid=1 -> PDHD APA0 plane2layer swap)
  np04hd-6paths        -1.000 / 400 ns
  PDVD norminal         0.000 / 0 ns     <-- BROKEN wire-0 (pitchpos=0) path (integral 0 not -1)
  PDVD imbalance3p     -1.000 / 2200 ns  <-- ~5.5x too broad
  PDVD 3view           -0.947 / 7800 ns  <-- ~20x too broad

TWO FR problems:
1) All PDVD collection responses are 5-20x BROADER than the normal 400 ns (dune/PDHD). This
   broad low-peak collection is what deconvolves too weak to pass the 5-sigma troi_col
   threshold (the sim+SP collection failure; affects imbalance3p too, so it is NOT specific
   to the norminal broken path).
2) The PDVD 'norminal' FR additionally has a BROKEN collection path exactly at pitchpos=0
   (integral 0 instead of -1); its off-center collecting paths (pitchpos -0.51..-2.55) are
   fine. imbalance3p has pitchpos=0 -> -1 correctly.

Both are field-response FILE issues (Garfield generation), NOT WCT-config/elec/filters.
Multi-page PDF written to xerosere/fr-responses.pdf (page/FR, subplot/plane, wire-0..4
responses vs time, legend = wire# + integral) for expert eyeballing. Script committed to main
(0a5f5fc).

comments.author: Brett Viren
comments.text:
RESOLVED (provisional): the PDVD collection 'crazy' response is now understood as PHYSICAL -- the CRP collection electrode is strips on stacked PCBs with thru-hole loop-back collection, giving a genuinely broad field response that ER convolution partly smooths. Not an FR bug (aside from the norminal pitchpos=0 zero-integral path, which the experts will review).

FIX applied: lowered PDVD sigproc.troi_col_th_factor 5.0 -> 2.5 in both trees (dune-config 379bad6, wire-cell-phlex a8e1aa0). This recovers the low-amplitude collection on the bare-OmnibusSigProc path: W-plane SP ROI traces 0 -> ~500/event, img_sp 0 -> 21 charged blobs. Threshold scan (norminal FR): 5.0->0, 3.0->270, 2.5->416, 2.0->819 W traces; 2.5 chosen (best imaging, less noise than 2.0). Provisional; dunereco keeps 5.0 with DNNROI.

SEPARATE issue now surfaced (was masked by img_sp=0): spdir pdvd img_splat BlobDepoFill assigns all-zero charge -- the depofill_time_offset (run.sh toffset=63000) is PDHD-calibrated; run.sh already notes PDVD reuses it 'pending its own calibration'. Needs a PDVD-specific toffset. Tracked separately.

title: B.4 Build libspng.so target + migrate WCT SPNG nodes to link it
description:
Build system: produce the `libspng.so` target (CMake) and/or a standalone
repository, and migrate the WCT SPNG `INode` glue to link against it (replacing
in-tree core compilation). Ensure both the WCT build and a WCT-free build of
`libspng` work.

title: B.3 Resolve deferred WCT-coupling debts in the SPNG core
description:
Resolve the WCT-coupling debts deferred during simng development (each filed as
a follow-up per the epic's relaxation policy): remove or re-abstract the
specific spots where core code reached into WCT to avoid duplication, so the
core is genuinely WCT-independent.

title: B.2 Define libspng public API + header layout (no WCT dependency)
description:
Define the `libspng` public API and header layout: pure `torch::Tensor` /
plain-data signatures, no `WireCell::Configuration`, no NamedFactory, no other
WCT headers. Decide namespacing, error-handling, and the `ITorchSpectrum`-style
seams that survive into the library.

title: B.1 Core/glue seam inventory across sigproc + sim; list of coupling debts
description:
Inventory and finalize the config-free core vs WCT-glue seam across the full
SPNG codebase (existing sigproc core + the new simng core), producing the
definitive list of files/symbols that belong in `libspng` vs stay as WCT glue,
and the list of accumulated WCT-coupling debts to resolve. Builds on simng F0.4.

title: libspng: extract config-free SPNG torch core (sigproc + sim) into a standalone library
description:
Extract the config-free *core* SPNG libtorch code — covering both signal
processing and the new simulation algorithms (see the simng epic) — into a
standalone `libspng.so` library that does **not** depend on wire-cell-toolkit.
The WCT SPNG `INode` glue then links against `libspng.so`.

## Motivation

SPNG already separates reusable torch math (`Convo.h`, `DFT.h`, `TorchLMN.h`,
`Util.h`, `TensorTools.h`) from WCT `IConfigurable`/`INode` glue, and the
`ITorchSpectrum` interface is a clean pure-torch seam. The simng epic is being
written to the same discipline (config-free core vs thin TDM nodes). Once both
sigproc and sim core exist in factored form, they can be lifted out so the
numerical library is usable without WCT's data-flow engine, configuration
system, or dependency stack.

## Scope

- Inventory and finalize the core/glue seam across sigproc + sim core.
- Define the `libspng` public API and headers (tensor/plain-data in, tensor
  out; no `WireCell::Configuration`, no NamedFactory, no other WCT headers).
- Build system: a `libspng.so` target (and/or standalone repo) and migrate the
  WCT SPNG nodes to link it.
- Resolve the WCT-coupling debts deliberately deferred during simng (the
  "relax the separation + file a follow-up" items) — this epic is their home.
- Packaging (Spack recipe) if it becomes a standalone repo.

## Relationship

Depends on the simng epic establishing the core-vs-glue layout (F0.4) and
implementing the sim core (F1). This epic is intentionally future-facing;
it collects the extraction work rather than blocking simng progress.

title: F2.3 Depo-transform / convolution node per plane (reuse ResponseKernel + KernelConvolve)
description:
Per-plane TDM depo-transform node producing induced current/voltage by reusing
`SPNGResponseKernel` (FR(x)ER `ITorchSpectrum`, already carries the ADC-count
scale) + `SPNGKernelConvolve` / F1.6 core. Node marshals the response provider
+ plane selection; math is reused. Includes the sim response/spectrum provider
glue (an `ITorchSpectrum` for the field response tensor from F1.5) if not
already covered by `SPNGResponseKernel`.

title: F2.2 Charge/raster node(s) per plane (point + segment)
description:
Per-plane TDM node(s) turning depos/segments into accumulated grid charge:
wrap F1.2 (point raster) and F1.4 (segment quadrature) + F1.3 accumulation.
One node instance per wire plane, producing the dense/block-sparse charge
tensor. Thin glue over core.

title: F2.1 Drift node (TDM)
description:
TDM drift node wrapping F1.1 core: `ITorchTensorSet` depo-tensor in/out,
marshalling config (`DL`,`DT`,`lifetime`,`fluctuate`,`speed`,`toffset`,
`xregions`) via Boost.Hana and delegating to the core. Built on
`TorchFunctionNode`. No physics in the node body.

title: F1.8 Core: digitization (gain/baseline/linear-transfer/saturate/floor)
description:
Core digitization as a tensor op: `adc = gain*voltage + baseline` mapped
through a linear transfer `fullscale -> [0, 2^resolution-1]` with saturation
clamp and floor/round selection, operating on the dense per-plane
(channel x tick) array. Mirror `gen/src/Digitizer.cxx` (but the dense array is
the natural target). Config-free (takes gain/baseline/fullscale/resolution as
plain args).

title: F1.7 Core: noise generation kernel (incoherent + coherent, mode=sqrt(2/pi)mu, Hermitian, iDFT)
description:
Core noise generation: from a mean amplitude spectrum mu compute mode
sigma = sqrt(2/pi)*mu, draw a complex spectrum with real/imag each ~N(0,sigma),
enforce Hermitian symmetry (real DC + Nyquist), inverse-DFT to a waveform.
Provide incoherent (per-row) and coherent (per-group, shared waveform)
variants and spectrum resampling to the target nsamples/tick. Mirror
`gen/docs/noise.org` + `gen/src/{AddNoise,Noise,EmpiricalNoiseModel,
GroupNoiseModel}.cxx`; respect the mean-vs-mode subtlety. Config-free (takes
spectra tensors).

title: F1.6 Core: charge->current convolution (reuse Convo/KernelConvolve; laced impact strategy)
description:
Core convolution of grid charge with the response tensor to induced
current/voltage, reusing `Convo.h` (`convo_spec`/`linear_shape`) and the
`SPNGKernelConvolve` engine rather than re-deriving FFT convolution. Implement
the interlaced/"laced" impact-strided strategy (tred `convo.interlaced_symm_v2`:
roll/pad/FFT/multiply/iFFT/sum over impact positions) so multiple impact
positions per pitch are handled in one pass. Config-free.

title: F1.5 Core: detector response tensor (2D per-plane FR(x)ER) + 3D response extension
description:
Core detector-response representation as torch tensors: build the per-plane
2D (impact-position x tick) response array (FR resampled from FR-period to
readout tick + convolved with electronics response, exploiting mirror symmetry)
from `Response::Schema`/`as_array` and `PlaneImpactResponse` semantics; and
support tred's 3D response layout (`ndlarsim`/`quadrant_copy`, interlaced impact
layout) as an extension. Reuse `TorchLMN` for resampling. Config-free (takes
loaded response data / tensors, not filenames).

title: F1.4 Core: line-segment charge model + Gauss-Legendre quadrature (from tred)
description:
Port tred's line-segment ionization model + Gaussian quadrature: the
closed-form charge density of a uniformly-charged 3D segment convolved with an
anisotropic Gaussian (`qline_diff3D`, exp x erf), the point fallback
(`qpoint_diff3D`) with `too_short` switch, and Gauss-Legendre quadrature onto
grid points (`create_wu_block` weights x interpolation, `eval_qeff` via grouped
conv3d), public `compute_qeff`. Source: `reference/tred/src/tred/raster/steps.py`.
Adds a segment depo model alongside point depos.

title: F1.2 Core: point-depo Gaussian erf-binned rasterization to (pitch x time) grid
description:
Core rasterization of point depos onto a (pitch x time) grid as an
erf-bin-integrated 2D Gaussian patch (outer product of two 1D binned
Gaussians), with optional charge-conserving fluctuation. Equivalent to
`gen/src/GaussianDiffusion.cxx` / `BinnedDiffusion_transform.cxx` and tred
`raster/depos.py::binned`. Reuse `Util::gaussian1d`. Output as the block-sparse
box representation from F1.3.

title: F5 Validation, parity vs gen/, and tests
description:
Validate the simng chain against the OG `gen/` implementation and add the
test/benchmark infrastructure: parity vs `DepoTransform`/`Digitizer`/
`AddNoise` on a reference detector, unit tests for core primitives and nodes,
and CPU/GPU correctness + performance benchmarks.

title: F4 Jsonnet config + subgraph assembly + detector integration
description:
Provide the Jsonnet configuration and subgraph assembly for the new sim node
chain following SPNG's layered config model (detector/tpc/control objects,
per-node factory functions, subgraph factories, top-level closures), wiring
per-plane fan-out/fan-in and integrating with detector configs and OG-frame
interop (`SPNGFrameToTdm`/`SPNGTdmToFrame`).

title: F3 Dynamic batching / rebatching between sim layers
description:
Map tred's dynamic batching into the node chain: allow each sim layer to
process a different batch depth, with zero-copy `narrow`-style buffering and
`concat`+scatter-add accumulation converting between layers, tuned against a
peak-memory budget to maximize GPU utilization. Analog of tred's
`batch_scheme` + `iter_chunk_block`/`iter_tensor_chunks` + `concat_blocks` +
`chunking.accumulate` (`reference/tred/plots/graph_effq.py`).

title: F2 SPNG TDM sim nodes (thin glue), per-plane
description:
Implement the SPNG TDM simulation *nodes* as thin gatekeepers between WCT
configuration and tensor I/O, built on `TorchFunctionNode`/`TensorFilter` and
following the "more, smaller nodes" rule (e.g. per-plane). Node bodies only
marshal config <-> `ITorchTensorSet` and delegate math to F1 core functions

title: wct-metrics bee: Bee zip export — true depos + sampled SP/splat blobs as point clouds

ROOT CAUSE of SP 'blips' found (touchstone experiment, pdhd APA0, 10 events).

The phlex sim+sigproc pipeline ADDS noise (AddNoise) but has NO Noise Filter (NF)
stage before OmnibusSigProc. The reference WCT chain (test-pdsp-simsn-nfsp.bats) runs
AddNoise -> Digitizer -> NF(OmnibusNoiseFilter+OmniChannelNoiseDB) -> SP. Our config
(BOTH devel/wire-cell-phlex/cfg/dune/wct AND devel/dune-config/cfg/dune/wct) omits NF
entirely (grep: no OmnibusNoiseFilter/OmniChannelNoiseDB/chndb anywhere; per_chan_resp='').

sim-sigproc.jsonnet and re-ran spdir osp pdhd:

  no-noise:            8437                 7638          1164   (splat unchanged)

unfiltered noise. FIX: add an NF stage (OmnibusNoiseFilter + channel-noise DB) between
Digitizer and OmnibusSigProc, matching pgrapher/experiment/pdsp nf.jsonnet+chndb-*.

tiling already tracked by this issue.

title: NamedFactory thread-safety for concurrent WCT Main islands (exec-time factory queries vs init writes)
description:
## Context

Upstream: https://github.com/WireCell/wire-cell-toolkit/issues/501

WCT's `NamedFactory.h` (util) exposes the global factory machinery through
process-global singletons: one `NamedFactoryRegistry<IType>` per interface type
(`Singleton<...>`) and one `NamedFactory<Concrete>` per concrete type. These are
shared across **all** `WireCell::Main` objects, so when multiple Mains run as
Phlex "islands" on different TBB worker threads, they read and write the *same*
containers. The scenario of concern: one Main is executing (doing factory
queries) while another Main hits its first execution and initializes,
mutating the shared containers.

Relevant background (Singleton/PluginManager already read):
- `Singleton<T>::Instance()` uses a function-local static → singleton *creation*
  is race-free (C++11 magic statics). Not a problem.
- `PluginManager` holds an unprotected `std::map<std::string,Plugin*> m_plugins`,
  reached on the `lookup_factory` cache-miss path.

## Shared mutable state (none internally synchronized)

| Container | Type | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `NamedFactory::m_objects` | `unordered_map` | `create()` / `instance(create=true)` |
| `NamedFactoryRegistry::m_lookup` | `unordered_map` | `associate()` (static init) **and** `lookup_factory()` cache-miss (runtime) |
| `NamedFactoryRegistry::m_known_types` | `set` | `hello()` (static init / dlopen) |
| `PluginManager::m_plugins` | `map` | `add()` |

## Findings from the code audit

**No accidental-insert bug.** Every query path uses `.find()`, never
`operator[]`, for lookups — `NamedFactory::find` (95), `create` (106),
`lookup_factory` (186), `known_classes` (279). A pure query never inserts a
default-constructed entry. Good.

**Method classification by side effect:**
1. Pure reads: `NamedFactory::find`; `instance(create=false)`; the
   `Factory::find/find_maybe/find_tn/find_maybe_tn` family.
2. Write-on-miss / read-on-hit: `create`, `instance(create=true)`, `lookup`,
   `lookup_tn`. If the target already exists, the fast path is a read-only
   `.find()` — the "side effect suppressed" case.
3. **Always potentially writes regardless of the create flag:**
   `lookup_factory` caches on miss (`m_lookup[classname]=fptr`) and touches
   `PluginManager`. So even a `find` is not purely read-only the *first* time a
   given classname's factory is resolved.

**The real hazard.** `unordered_map`/`map`/`set` have no internal
synchronization; a concurrent reader + writer on the same container is a data
race (an insert can rehash and invalidate nodes mid-read) → UB. The proposed
cross-Main init mutex serializes writer-vs-writer, but a Main that is
*executing* does not hold that mutex, so writer(init)-vs-reader(exec) is
unprotected. Therefore: "achieve safety by ensuring the create side effect does
not fire" (target already populated) is **necessary but not sufficient** — it
removes the executing Main's own writes but it still reads a container another
Main's init is writing. A query is safe only when its target is fully
pre-populated AND no other Main is concurrently initializing.

## Options evaluated

**Option 1 — one global reader/writer lock (phase separation).** Make the
cross-Main init lock a process-wide `std::shared_mutex`: Main init takes it
exclusively, every exec-time query takes it shared. Robust in principle but
requires routing *all* factory queries (buried deep in pipeline node
`execute()`s) through the shared lock — hard to guarantee coverage — and
serializes init against all execution.

**Option 2 — fine-grained locks inside NamedFactory.** Add a mutex to
`NamedFactory<Type>` (guards `m_objects`), `NamedFactoryRegistry<IType>`
(guards `m_lookup` + `m_known_types`), and `PluginManager` (guards `m_plugins`).
Reads take a shared/lock, writes take exclusive; `lookup_factory` uses a
double-checked pattern (shared read, drop, exclusive re-check, insert). Fits
Phlex's staggered lazy-first-execution model best.

Design refinements for Option 2:
- **Use `std::mutex`, not `std::shared_mutex`.** Exec-phase factory access is
  rare, so concurrent readers are rare; shared_mutex's reader-count cache-line
  contention and heavier acquire cost lose to a plain mutex here.
- **Scope the exclusive section to the map mutation only** — never hold it
  across `new Type` or the plugin `dlopen` (long blocks + possible recursion/
  deadlock if a ctor re-enters `Factory::find`). Construct outside the lock and
  accept that two racing misses may both construct, discarding the loser
  (harmless for WCT's construct-then-configure model).
- **Policy:** all of this is in `util`, which takes NO new external deps ever —
  so `tbb::concurrent_hash_map` etc. are out; `std::mutex` (stdlib) is fine.

**Runtime speed / build-switch question (the key decision).**
- Uncontended `std::mutex` lock/unlock (~10–25 ns) is comparable to a warm
  string-keyed `unordered_map::find`, so it can ~double a warm lookup's cost. A
  distinct-phase single-threaded `wire-cell` CLI would pay this on every query
  for a guarantee it doesn't need.
- **Do NOT gate this with a compile-time switch.** `NamedFactory.h` is a
  template header included across every plugin, and its objects cross `dlopen`
  boundaries. A flag that adds/removes a mutex member changes `sizeof`/layout of
  `NamedFactory<Foo>` between TUs built with vs without it → **ODR violation →
  silent memory corruption** when a mismatched plugin loads. This is a severe
  trap in the DUNE ecosystem where plugins are built separately.
- **Prefer a runtime switch:** keep the mutex member *always present* (stable
  ABI, plugins always compatible) and gate the *behavior* on a process-global
  `std::atomic<bool>` set once at startup before any threads spawn (Phlex sets
  true; plain CLIs leave false). Cost when off = one relaxed load + a predicted
  branch — effectively free.
- Only if a benchmark proves the runtime version too slow should a compile-time
  switch be considered, and then it must be an ecosystem-wide, non-optional
  flag baked into installed headers plus a load-time guard symbol so a
  mismatched plugin refuses to load.

**Option 3 (this issue's preferred direction) — fix the components + coarse
Phlex-side mutex.** Audit and fix all WCT components so they only touch
`NamedFactory` during their init phase (`configure()`), never during exec, and
protect `WireCell::Main` initialize with a mutex in the Phlex algorithm. If no
component ever queries the factory during exec, there is no reader concurrent
with an init writer, so the shared containers can stay lock-free. This targets
the root cause rather than paying per-query locking forever. Some components
today *do* touch NamedFactory at exec time; those are the ones to fix. Option 3
and Option 2 are complementary: Option 3 removes the need for Option 2 in the
common case, and Option 2 (runtime-gated) can remain as a safety net.

## Acceptance

- Decision on approach: Option 3 (component audit + Phlex init mutex) as primary
  direction, with a documented position on whether runtime-gated Option 2 locks
  are also added as a backstop.
- If Option 3: an audit list of WCT components that touch `NamedFactory` outside
  `configure()`, with fixes moving those queries into init phase.
- Confirmation that `WireCell::Main` initialize is protected by a mutex on the
  Phlex-algorithm side.
- Any NamedFactory changes: `util` gains no external deps; `std::mutex` only;
  runtime gate not compile-time; write critical sections minimally scoped.

title: Eliminate duplicate wire/channel pointer storage in AnodePlane/WirePlane/SimpleChannel
description: Hold one canonical set of IWire/IChannel pointers and derive the rest. Today the same pointers live in Gen::WirePlane::m_wires (gen/inc/WireCellGen/WirePlane.h:36), Gen::AnodePlane::m_c2wires (AnodePlane.h:43), and Aux::SimpleChannel::m_wires. Choose one owner (e.g. per-plane in WirePlane) and make the channel->wires and c2wires lookups views/indices into it. Remove dead Gen::WirePlane::m_bbox. Keep wcdoctest green.

title: Phase 2: parametric plane-geometry interface + migrate consumers off IWire/IChannel
description:
**Phase 2 — parametric plane-geometry interface + migrate consumers off
IWire/IChannel.** The usage audit shows the overwhelming majority of consumers
never call `ray()`; they need only plane-level parametric geometry (category B)
or the wire-index <-> channel-id association map (category C). Give them a
first-class *compact* interface so those paths never construct `IWire`/`IChannel`
at all, and migrate them.

## Design

Design a compact plane-geometry object exposing the "fundamental" parameter set
the user described: pitch vector + pitch origin + plane bounding box + wire-index
range/count + a wire-index<->channel-id map (+ the existing `raygrid()`). This is
close to `Pimpos` (util/inc/WireCellUtil/Pimpos.h:135-141) plus the channel map;
both `Pimpos` and `RayGrid::Coordinates` are already derivable from <=2
wires/plane + bbox (gen/src/AnodePlane.cxx:239, gen/src/AnodeFace.cxx:34-44). Back
it with the **same F2 provider** so there is one source of truth. Depends on F2.

## Consumer strategy (from the A/B/C catalog)

- **B (plane-parametric):** all gen/ transport (DepoTransform, DepoFluxSplat,
  DepoSplat, TruthTraceID, TruthSmearer, MultiDuctor, WireBoundedDepos),
  img/GridTiling + BlobDepoFill, clus/ and spng/ raygrid users, aux/ sampling —
  migrate to the compact interface + index->channel map instead of
  `plane->wires()`.
- **C (wire<->channel map):** sigproc/OmnibusSigProc, sigproc/ROI_refinement,
  img tiling/striping/clustering, clus/BlobSampler, PointTreeBuilding,
  DynamicPointCloud, TrackFitting — migrate to the wire-index / channel-map API.
- **A (per-wire ray):** gen/WireSummary, gen/EmpiricalNoiseModel,
  sigproc/OmniChannelNoiseDB, root/MagnifySink, spng/CellBasis + FrameToTdm,
  aux/ClusterHelpersJsonify, plus pointer-identity graph users
  (img/NaiveStriper, BlobClustering) — keep a per-wire ray accessor on the
  provider (or the lazy IWire from F2); ensure no path forces full
  materialization.

## Outcome

The hot simulation and imaging paths obtain geometry without ever allocating
per-wire/per-channel objects; the object model is a fallback for the small
category-A set; overall footprint and allocation churn drop further.

title: Phase 1: lazy/algorithmic IWire/IChannel backed by a shared geometry provider
description:
**Phase 1 — lazy/algorithmic IWire/IChannel backed by a shared geometry
provider.** Replace the heavyweight `Aux::SimpleWire`/`Aux::SimpleChannel`
(each ~80 B + a `Ray` that duplicates data already in `WireSchema::Store`, plus
shared_ptr control blocks) with lazy implementations that carry only an id and a
back-reference to a single geometry provider component. `IWire`/`IChannel`
methods then compute their return values on demand from the provider.

## Design

Introduce a wire-geometry *provider* that answers queries — `ray(wire_id)`,
`index`, `channel`, `planeid`, wires-of-channel, segment — from the compact,
already-shared `WireSchema::Store` (endpoints in `StoreDB::wires`) plus a
per-plane `Pimpos` and the data-driven channel map (`WireSchema::channels()`).
No per-wire heap objects. Reuse the existing `IWireSchema` component
(`Gen::WireSchemaFile`) and `Pimpos` rather than inventing new geometry math.
This provider is the shared implementation that F3 (Phase 2) also builds on.

## Rationale

Wire geometry is stored once in `WireSchema::StoreDB` then copied again into
every `SimpleWire::m_ray` (gen/src/AnodePlane.cxx:219-222). A lazy `IWire` that
holds `{id, provider*}` and derives `ray()` from the Store removes that entire
second copy and its control blocks. Wrapped-wire / multi-segment channels
(`channel_wire_collector_t`, gen/src/AnodePlane.cxx:78-102) must be handled by
the provider, not by retained vectors.

Depends on F1: while the collection accessors still return `const&`, the lazy
objects would be forced to cache full vectors, defeating the goal.

## Outcome

`Gen::AnodePlane::configure` builds the provider + lazy objects instead of
`SimpleWire`/`SimpleChannel`; duplicate storage is gone; Pimpos ownership is
fixed; measured footprint drops sharply at PDSP/DUNE-FD scale with byte-identical
outputs on existing goldens.

title: Interface modernization: stop returning const-ref collections from wire geometry interfaces
description:
**Interface modernization:** stop returning `const&` collections from the wire
geometry interfaces, then fix the resulting breakage. This is the prerequisite
that lets a lazy IWire/IChannel implementation (F2) actually shed memory.

## Rationale

`IChannel::wires()` (iface/inc/WireCellIface/IChannel.h:33),
`IWirePlane::wires()` (IWirePlane.h:29), and `IWirePlane::channels()`
(IWirePlane.h:33) return `const IWire::vector&` / `const IChannel::vector&`.
A const reference to a collection forces the implementation to *own* the full
vector for the object's lifetime, which defeats a lazy/algorithmic backing
store. The user explicitly flagged this as a design mistake to fix.

## Design tension to resolve

Some consumers rely on **stable `IWire*` pointer identity** as graph-node keys
(img/src/NaiveStriper.cxx, img/src/BlobClustering.cxx) — a by-value
materialization that returns fresh objects each call would break them. The new
signature (by-value vector vs. `std::span` vs. a lazy range/iterator) must be
chosen with those users in mind.

## Outcome

Geometry interfaces no longer force the implementation to retain full
collections; all consumers compile and `wcdoctest` stays green; the door is open
for F2's lazy objects.

title: Foundational: remove storage duplication and fix leaks in the current AnodePlane model (no interface change)
description:
**Foundational memory win with no interface change:** remove redundant duplicate
storage of wire/channel objects and fix the raw-pointer leaks in the current
`Gen::AnodePlane` object model. Independent of F1/F2/F3, low risk, and a useful
early reduction that also de-risks the larger refactors.

## Rationale (from the memory audit)

The same `IWire::pointer`s are stored in several places at once:
`Gen::WirePlane::m_wires` (gen/inc/WireCellGen/WirePlane.h:36),
`Gen::AnodePlane::m_c2wires` (gen/inc/WireCellGen/AnodePlane.h:43, an
`unordered_map<int, IWire::vector>` keyed by channel), and
`Aux::SimpleChannel::m_wires`. Ownership bugs compound the cost:
`Pimpos* pimpos = new Pimpos(...)` is leaked on reconfigure
(gen/src/AnodePlane.cxx:239), `Gen::WirePlane::m_pimpos` is a leaked raw pointer,
and `channel_wire_collector_t` deliberately never frees
(gen/src/AnodePlane.cxx:80-84). `Gen::WirePlane::m_bbox` is dead.

## Outcome

Fewer live copies of the wire/channel pointer vectors; correct ownership; a
measured reduction in per-detector footprint using only the current interfaces,
with identical outputs on existing goldens.

title: [epic] Scalable wire/channel geometry: shrink the IAnodePlane object model for DUNE FD
description:
Shrink the memory footprint of the WCT wire/channel geometry object model
(`IAnodePlane` / `IAnodeFace` / `IWirePlane` / `IWire` / `IChannel`) so it
scales from ProtoDUNE to DUNE far-detector sizes.

## Problem

`Gen::AnodePlane` (gen/) materializes one heavyweight heap object for **every
wire segment and every channel** in the detector. This is expensive at PDSP
scale and burdensome at DUNE-FD scale. Three things make it worse:

1. **Redundant geometry storage.** Wire endpoints are stored once as
   `WireSchema::Wire{Point tail, head}` in the shared `WireSchema::StoreDB`,
   then copied *again* as `Ray m_ray` inside every `Aux::SimpleWire`
   (~80 B/object + shared_ptr control block). The resulting `IWire::pointer`s
   are then held redundantly in several collections:
   `Gen::WirePlane::m_wires`, `Gen::AnodePlane::m_c2wires`, and
   `Aux::SimpleChannel::m_wires`.

2. **Silly provenance.** Wires files exhaustively list every wire segment even
   though they originate from an *algorithm* (wire-cell-python
   `wirecell-util gdml-to-wires`, gdml.py). WCT then must "regularize" that data
   at load — `WireSchema::load()` applies `order` / `direction` / `pitch`
   corrections (util/src/WireSchema.cxx:181-350) to restore uniform pitch,
   parallel wires, and orientation — precision lost across GDML->JSON->float and
   several intermediate files. Regenerating exhaustive data only to correct it
   is wasteful; the wire index and channel-ID association are also algorithmic.

3. **Interface flaw.** `IChannel::wires()`, `IWirePlane::wires()`, and
   `IWirePlane::channels()` return `const IWire::vector&` /
   `const IChannel::vector&`. Returning const references to collections forces
   the implementation to retain the full vectors in memory, defeating any lazy
   approach.

Crucially, **most consumers do not need the individual objects.** A usage audit
classifies consumers as:

- **A — genuinely needs per-wire `ray()`**: a small set, mostly wire-length or
  serialization (gen/WireSummary, gen/EmpiricalNoiseModel,
  sigproc/OmniChannelNoiseDB, root/MagnifySink, spng/CellBasis+FrameToTdm,
  aux/ClusterHelpersJsonify), plus pointer-identity graph users
  (img/NaiveStriper, img/BlobClustering).
- **B — only plane-level parametric geometry** (`Pimpos`, `raygrid()`, bbox,
  wire-index range, plane-X scalar): the bulk — all gen/ simulation transport,
  img/GridTiling, most clus/ and spng/ code, aux/ sampling.
- **C — only the wire-index <-> channel-id association map**: sigproc/OmnibusSigProc,
  sigproc/ROI_refinement, gen channel stamping, clus/BlobSampler,
  PointTreeBuilding, DynamicPointCloud, TrackFitting, img tiling.

Both `Pimpos` (gen/src/AnodePlane.cxx:239) and `RayGrid::Coordinates`
(gen/src/AnodeFace.cxx:34-44) are already derivable from <=2 wires/plane + a
bounding box. `Pimpos` (util/inc/WireCellUtil/Pimpos.h:135-141: pitch, origin,
3 axes, two Binnings) is essentially the compact per-plane parameter set the
phase-2 approach wants.

## Approach (features)

This epic groups four workstreams, wired so each feature is blocked by its
tasks and this epic is blocked by its features (dependency tree is the inverse
of the hierarchical epic->feature->task tree):

- **F0 (foundational, no interface change):** remove the redundant duplicate
  storage and fix the raw-pointer leaks in the current model. Low risk, early
  memory win, de-risks the rest.
- **F1 (interface modernization):** stop returning `const&` collections from the
  geometry interfaces; fix the resulting breakage. Prerequisite for a real lazy
  implementation.
- **F2 (Phase 1):** replace `SimpleWire`/`SimpleChannel` with lazy/algorithmic
  `IWire`/`IChannel` that carry only an id + a back-reference to a shared
  geometry provider; the provider computes `ray()`/index/channel on demand from
  the compact `WireSchema::Store` + `Pimpos` + channel map. Blocked by F1.
- **F3 (Phase 2):** give the category-B/C consumers a first-class *compact*
  plane-geometry + wire<->channel-map interface so they never construct
  `IWire`/`IChannel` at all; migrate them. Shares F2's provider as its backing
  implementation. Blocked by F2.

## Scope / references

Work happens in devel/wire-cell-toolkit (branch TBD). Key anchors:
gen/src/AnodePlane.cxx, gen/src/WirePlane.cxx, gen/src/AnodeFace.cxx,
aux/inc/WireCellAux/{SimpleWire,SimpleChannel}.h, util/src/WireSchema.cxx,
util/inc/WireCellUtil/Pimpos.h, iface/inc/WireCellIface/I{Wire,Channel,WirePlane,AnodeFace,AnodePlane}.h.

Note WCT project policy: interfaces and their consumers span many sub-packages;
changes must keep the full `wcdoctest` suite green and honor the plugin
no-inter-dependency and test-first rules.

title: Adopt m.make<AlgWrapper>() for WCT-island main-thread construct/init/finalize
description:
Evaluate and adopt the `m.make<AlgWrapper>()` idiom (suggested by a Phlex dev) for the
WCT-island lifecycle. Depends on the problem issue.

## Mechanism (verified against installed phlex 0.3.2)

`m.make<U>(args...)` -> `graph_proxy::bind_to<...,U>(args...)` ->
`std::make_shared<U>(std::forward<Args>(args)...)` (reference/phlex
phlex/core/graph_proxy.hpp). This runs SYNCHRONOUSLY inside PHLEX_REGISTER_ALGORITHMS:

- U's constructor runs on the MAIN THREAD during registration, before framework_graph
  execution and before any TBB worker task.
- The resulting `shared_ptr<U>` is owned by the node; `~U()` runs at graph/node-catalog
  teardown, also on the main thread => a symmetric main-thread finalize() point.
- Registering `.transform("name", &U::execute, ...)` makes it a BOUND class-method node
  (delegate.hpp real-instance path), replacing our current bare-lambda (void_tag) node
  that captures a `shared_ptr<Executor>`.

## Evaluation result

PROMISING as an idiom — adopt it — but necessary-but-not-sufficient for the resource
case. Specifically:

What it buys us:
1. A defined, symmetric main-thread finalize() via `~AlgWrapper` (dtor -> alg_.finalize()).
   We currently lack this; WCT Main teardown is implicit in a defaulted ~Executor.
   ddm-4or.4's initialize()-only proposal does not cover teardown.
2. Zero upstream change: available in the installed phlex 0.3.2 today. It makes the
   ddm-4or.4 upstream hook largely UNNECESSARY for our go-jsonnet crash (already fixed
   by ctor-time init). The wrapper is a cleaner, more explicit spelling of
   "construct on the main thread", aligned with the Phlex dev's guidance.
3. A structural home (the wrapper) for a future split-init needed by the resource case.

What it does NOT solve (key limitation):
- Sub-problem B. The wrapper ctor runs at REGISTRATION, before any product/resource
  arrives, so `alg_.initialize()` there cannot configure AnodePlane (needs the
  execution-time WireSchema resource). Same pre-execution limitation as ddm-4or.4's
  proposed hook. Restoring FacadeWireSchema additionally requires:
    (a) Phlex resource delivery (ddm-999) to bring WireSchema in as a serialized
        ("limited") resource, and
    (b) splitting WCT `Main::initialize()` into compile-config-on-main-thread (ctor)
        + instantiate/configure-once-resource-present (first execute()), the latter
        guarded by std::call_once AND run under the framework's serialized/limited
        resource access so the cross-island WCT-factory configure has no race.
  So the wrapper is the container in which B's split-init lives, not a fix for B.

Verdict: adopt `m.make<>` for WCT islands now (finalize() benefit + structural home);
keep B gated on ddm-999.

## Implementation steps

1. Make the node object a wrapper (or the Executor itself). In register_shapes.hpp,
   replace `std::make_shared<FunctionExecutor<...>>(cfg)` + capturing lambda with
   `m.make<Wrapper>(cfg).transform(node, &Wrapper::execute, serial).input_family(...)
   .output_...`. Preserve today's per-shape adapters (the fan pack/unpack and
   tuple<Data<Out>...> handling currently in the lambdas) as `Wrapper::execute`
   member(s) / thin methods. Do the observe (sink) and provide (source) equivalents.
2. Split Executor into explicit initialize()/finalize(): ctor calls initialize()
   (today's initialize_now() body); dtor calls finalize() (explicit WCT Main teardown,
   currently defaulted). Confirm WireCell::Main exposes/needs an explicit finalize or
   terminate and wire it; ensure it runs exactly once per island on the main thread.
3. Confirm the bound-node path: `.transform(name, &Wrapper::execute)` satisfies phlex
   is_transform_like for pointer-to-member; handle multi-output (tuple) and fan arity
   via member templates or per-N methods; verify observe/provide member-fn overloads.
4. Exception semantics: a throwing wrapper ctor propagates through make_shared during
   registration (NOT via the registration_api errors_ vector). Confirm phlex plugin
   load surfaces it cleanly; decide keep-throwing vs. capture-into-config-errors.
5. Regression: run the split full-chain smoke tests at DEFAULT parallelism
   (devel/wire-cell-phlex-arrow/test/run-fullchain-split.sh, no -j 1) — must pass and
   show finalize() running once per island at teardown. This also confirms the
   go-jsonnet crash stays fixed under the bound-node refactor.
6. (Deferred; gated by ddm-999) Re-enable FacadeWireSchema on top of the wrapper via
   split-init: compile config in ctor; on first execute() carrying the WireSchema
   resource, register_store + run the resource-dependent configure under a
   serialized/"limited" resource + std::call_once. Track as its own follow-up.

## Acceptance

- Documented decision (this task) that `m.make<>` is adopted for WCT islands, with the
  mechanism and limitation above.
- register_shapes.hpp executors registered as bound class-method nodes via `m.make<>`,
  with a main-thread finalize() firing once per island; split smoke tests pass at
  default -j.
- Resource-backed FacadeWireSchema restoration explicitly deferred to a ddm-999-gated
  follow-up, with the split-init plan recorded.

comments.author: Brett Viren
comments.text: Correction after reading phlex delegate.hpp (0.3.2): m.make<AlgWrapper>().transform(&AlgWrapper::execute) is NOT lifecycle-different from the current lambda m.transform() form in register_shapes.hpp register_function(). Both delegate() overloads produce a shared_ptr captured inside a std::function node body (algorithm_bits::bound_): the lambda form via delegate(shared_ptr<void_tag>, f); the make form via delegate(shared_ptr<T>, &T::f) = std::function{[t=obj,f](args){return ((*t).*f)(args);}}. Consequences: (1) construction/initialize timing is IDENTICAL - both std::make_shared run synchronously in the same PHLEX_REGISTER_ALGORITHMS body on the main thread before execution; our Executor already inits in its ctor via initialize_now(), so AlgWrapper's alg_.initialize() lands at the same point. (2) destruction/finalize is IDENTICAL - same shared_ptr-in-std::function ownership, released at node_catalog/framework_graph teardown on the main thread; a finalize() in ~Executor fires at the same moment in both forms. Therefore the earlier 'main-thread finalize() we currently lack' bullet is WRONG: we can get finalize() today by putting it in ~Executor. The ONLY real difference: the make<T> form gives phlex a TYPED bound object (delegate(shared_ptr<T>,...)), which is the sole seam a future phlex main-thread initialize()/finalize() hook (ddm-4or.4) could detect and call - detection keys on the concrete type, so a void_tag lambda node is structurally excluded. Net: adopt make<AlgWrapper> for FUTURE hook-eligibility and structure, NOT for any present-day lifecycle change.

comments.author: Brett Viren
comments.text: Added a runnable illustration at devel/phlexed/lifecycle/ (README.md + run.sh). It builds four trivial Phlex plugins sharing ONE core class (lifecycle::Worker, standing in for the WCT Executor) and registers it two ways: (A) lambda + shared_ptr as in wire-cell-phlex register_function(), node 'lam'; (B) m.make<AlgWrapper>().transform(&AlgWrapper::execute), node 'mak'. Each of ctor/initialize/execute/finalize/dtor prints its thread id + MAIN-vs-worker. Three topologies (chain, swapped, diamond) x -j sweep, per-node concurrency fixed at serial(1). Empirical result confirms the analysis: for BOTH styles ctor+initialize run on MAIN at registration, execute runs on TBB workers when -j>1 (diamond shows lam+mak on distinct worker tids concurrently; note the main thread also serves as a worker so an execute line may still read MAIN), and finalize+dtor run on MAIN at teardown. I.e. the two styles are lifecycle-equivalent today; the only real difference (typed bound object as a seam for a future ddm-4or.4 main-thread hook) is not observable at runtime. Demo deliberately does NOT address sub-problem B (execution-time resource), matching ddm-4or.5.

title: Phlex lifecycle vs. threads for WCT islands: main-thread init/finalize and execution-time resource delivery
description:
## Context

A "WCT island" is a Phlex node whose body is a `wcphlex::Executor` driving a full
WCT sub-graph (devel/wire-cell-phlex). Islands run on TBB worker threads. WCT's
global machinery — the string-keyed `NamedFactoryRegistry`/`PluginManager` and the
embedded go-jsonnet (cgo) config engine — is NOT thread-safe, and WCT "service like"
components have configure-time ordering dependencies (e.g. `AnodePlane::configure()`
consumes an `IWireSchema` during `WireCell::Main::initialize()`). In a pure-WCT job
that ordering is guaranteed by the config's topological sort on the single main
thread. In Phlex there is no serialized main-thread entry point for island bodies.

This issue records the general Phlex-lifecycle-vs-threads problem for WCT islands and
its two coupled sub-problems.

## Sub-problem A — main-thread, once-only construct / initialize / finalize

WCT `Main::initialize()` (which triggers go-jsonnet cgo evaluation + global-factory
configure) must run once, on the main thread, never concurrently across islands.

CURRENT STATE (verified 2026-08-18): this is already handled by construction-time
initialization. `Executor::initialize_now()` (m_wcmain.initialize() + virtual
initialize_ports()) is called as the final step of each concrete executor's
constructor, and register_shapes.hpp constructs executors via
`std::make_shared<Executor>(config)` during `PHLEX_REGISTER_ALGORITHMS` — i.e. on the
main thread, serially, before graph execution. See Executor.hpp / Executor.cpp:138
("No locking is required: module construction is serial"). So the concurrent
go-jsonnet cgo crash tracked in ddm-4or.4 is already mitigated for our executors by
ctor-time init, WITHOUT the upstream initialize() hook.

Residual gap in A: there is no defined main-thread finalize()/teardown hook. WCT Main
teardown is implicit in `~Executor` (defaulted). ddm-4or.4's initialize()-only
proposal does not cover teardown either.

## Sub-problem B — resource-backed "service like" component (the part we backed off)

We wanted a WCT service-like component that exposes a Phlex "resource" data product to
a WCT sub-graph: `FacadeWireSchema` feeds the wire geometry into WCT's configure-time
`IWireSchema` service so `AnodePlane::configure()` can consume it. The geometry /
channel-map arrives as an EXECUTION-TIME Phlex product (a "resource"), delivered like a
normal data-flow product on the trailing algorithm argument.

This is fundamentally incompatible with the sub-problem-A fix. `AnodePlane::configure()`
runs during `m_wcmain.initialize()`, which now runs at CONSTRUCTION — before any
run-time product can arrive. FacadeWireSchema is therefore currently DISABLED (not
built); see the "Geometry-as-PHLEX-product" note in Executor.hpp.

The bind: ctor-time init is thread-safe but too early to see the resource; deferring
init to the first `execute()` sees the resource but reintroduces cross-island races
over WCT's non-thread-safe global factory (and previously the go-jsonnet cgo crash).
There is no main-thread, post-construction entry point that ALSO carries the
execution-time resource datum.

## Relationships

- ddm-4or.4 — proposed upstream main-thread initialize() hook. Note it runs BEFORE
  execution, so it does not by itself deliver the resource datum needed for B; and
  ctor-time init already covers the go-jsonnet crash it targets.
- ddm-999 — await Phlex resources API (m.resource / handle->make); the framework
  serializes access to "limited" (thread-unsafe/mutable) resources. This is the
  intended native vehicle for B.
- ddm-3j8.1.13 / ddm-3j8.1.14 — channel-map as a parse-once shared/resource object.

## Acceptance

A clear written statement of the two sub-problems (this issue) plus a decision on the
`m.make<AlgWrapper>()` idiom and a concrete implementation path (dependent task) for
adopting main-thread construct/initialize/finalize and for eventually restoring the
resource-backed FacadeWireSchema on top of it.

title: SPDIR: wire SPNG signal-processing island (sim-spng.jsonnet) for run.sh sp=spng
description: run.sh accepts sp=osp|spng and detector=pdhd|pdvd via token substitution; osp works. spng currently skips (77) because there is no phlex island config for SPNG. SPNG (devel/wire-cell-toolkit/spng) is a torch/TensorSet subsystem (SPNGDecon/CrossViews/etc, FrameToTorchSet, SPNGTdmToFrame). Need a boundary-form island config dune/wct/job/sim-spng.jsonnet (DepoSetBoundarySource -> DepoTransform+Digitizer -> SPNG decon -> SPNGTdmToFrame -> FrameBoundarySink), the WireCellSpng plugin, and the spng cfg tree on WIRECELL_PATH. Adapt from spng/cfg/spng/{adc-to-spng-simple,subgraphs}.jsonnet. Substantial (torch runtime + boundary bridging).

title: edep-phlex: LineGen coords='wires' support
description: Add per-wire-plane angle interpretation to LineGen. For coords='wires', each (theta_y,theta_xz) pair yields 3 events (one global direction per plane) via dir_glb = R_p^T . dir_wp, where R_p rotates about drift-X by each plane's wire angle. Blocked on deciding how to supply per-plane wire directions to edep-phlex WITHOUT a wire-cell-toolkit dependency (candidate: a wire_angles:[a0,a1,a2] config param computed upstream). Currently LineGen throws for coords='wires'.

title: Photon+electron test on LArSoft-flavored GDML with optical properties
description: Once the LArSoft-flavored protodunehd GDML that ALSO carries LAr optical properties (RINDEX, SCINTILLATIONYIELD*, etc.) and a SurfaceDetector/photon-detector volume is available (a colleague is producing it, 2026-08), wire it into an integration test that produces BOTH detected optical photons AND field-driven ionization electrons on a realistic geometry.
design:
The scaffolding already exists (added 2026-08-13, wire-cell-phlex-arrow commit 44206b4):
- devel/wire-cell-phlex-arrow/test/run-optical-photons.sh
- test/smoke-optical-photons.jsonnet
- test/check-optical-photons.py  (geometry-agnostic: asserts non-empty photons table + physical/finite ionization split)
- test/optical-lar.gdml  (SYNTHETIC stand-in to be REPLACED by the real GDML)

Swap steps when the real GDML lands:
1. Point smoke-optical-photons.jsonnet @GDML@ at the new LArSoft+optical GDML (or hardcode as the pdhd tests do); retire optical-lar.gdml.
2. Keep the job 'macro' knobs -- they are edep-sim defaults, geometry-independent:
     /process/optical/scintillation/setStackPhotons true
     /process/optical/boundary/setInvokeSD true
3. Re-tune check-optical-photons.py MIN_PHOTON_HITS (currently 10) for the real scintillation yield; consider a low-energy primary (e.g. 10 MeV e-) to keep Geant4 optical transport cheap.

Context: the pdhd full-chain shows ZERO photons purely by configuration (no optical properties, no SurfaceDetector, edep-sim defaults disable photon stacking) -- NOT a bug. See ddm-496 closing notes.
acceptance_criteria: An integration test runs on the LArSoft-flavored optical GDML and asserts the observables hold both a non-empty 'photons' table and a physical, finite ionization split; optical-lar.gdml stand-in removed.

title: dune-config: end-to-end noise-model run on real PDHD/PDVD DAQ files + golden/smoke test
description:
End-to-end: run the noise-model job on a real DUNE DAQ HDF5 file (a PDHD run and
a PDVD run, using data under data/) and confirm it produces physically-plausible
average noise half-spectra JSON from NoiseModeler.  Add a dune-config test
(golden or structural check) covering the assembled Phlex+WCT config and, where
data is available, a runtime smoke test of the produced spectra.

Correctness of the offline channel ids feeding the noise groups depends on the
real-fragment channel-map validation (ddm-3j8.1.16).  Depends on the WCT body,
the Phlex side-effect workflow, the DAQ input wiring, the sub-detector
abstraction, and the sub-detector coordination tasks.

title: dune-config: coordinate configured vs. file-present sub-detectors; fan noise-model over the intersection
description:
The "something extra": reconcile the CONFIGURED sub-detector set (the detector's
anodes/APAs/CRPs selected for the job) against the sub-detectors actually PRESENT
in a given input DAQ HDF5 file, and build the noise-model graph over the
intersection.

A DAQ HDF5 file exposes only some readout units (SourceIDs / DetIDs / Fragments);
a job configured for a whole detector must not assume all its sub-detectors are
present.  Design + implement the coordination:
  * Determine which sub-detectors the input file contains (from the DAQ file
    layout / SourceID enumeration in dune-daq-hdf, or a job-config-supplied
    manifest), and map SourceID/DetID -> the detector schema's anode ident.
  * Fan/iterate the noise-model body over the present-and-configured sub-detector
    set (reuse the pg.fan multi-anode assembly, ddm-4pz.7), producing per-group
    or per-sub-detector NoiseModeler output.
  * Decide config ergonomics: explicit sub-detector list in job config vs.
    file-driven discovery, and how mismatches are reported.

Depends on the channel-map parse-once object (ddm-3j8.1.13) and multi-anode
assembly (ddm-4pz.7); relates the channel-map resource delivery (ddm-3j8.1.14).
Builds on the sub-detector abstraction task.

title: dune-config: wire raw DUNE DAQ HDF5 input (daq-hdf source) into the noise-model workflow
description:
Wire the real daq-hdf input kind (phlex/sources.jsonnet has it as a STUB) into
the noise-model workflow, so the job reads raw DUNE DAQ HDF5 and provides decoded
IFrames.  This consumes the DAQ read path built under ddm-3j8.1: the Phlex
DUNE-DAQ HDF5 source (ddm-3j8.1.6), dune-daq-hdf/-codec/-wct bridge, and the
channel-map delivery as a Phlex resource (ddm-3j8.1.14 / parse-once object
ddm-3j8.1.13).

Un-stub the "daq-hdf" source entry (cpp module + its generic IO config) and make
a noise-model workflow assemble+run over a DAQ file.  HARD-GATED on the Phlex
DAQ source module (ddm-3j8.1.6) existing; until then this task tracks the
integration shape.

title: dune-config: Phlex side-effect (sink-terminated) workflow variant for the noise-model job
description:
Add a Phlex workflow variant (phlex/workflow.jsonnet + sinks.jsonnet) for a
SIDE-EFFECT / sink-terminated job: a source module feeds one WCT executor module
that runs the noise-model WCT body, with NO downstream phlex sink module (the
WCT graph terminates in NoiseModeler and writes JSON as its side effect).

Concretely:
  * A new executor flow "frame_to_sink" (or "frame_to_none"): the executor cpp
    is a frame-consuming module whose WCT body is sink-terminated; there is no
    output product/sink to attach.
  * The workflow builder omits the sink module and threads the NoiseModeler
    `outname` (the noise-spectra JSON path) down to the WCT body as a TLA.
  * Keep the phlex/wct domain separation: the workflow only REFERENCES the WCT
    job by filename and passes detector/variant/anode/outname as TLAs.

Note the phlex-provider-needs-consumer constraint: a terminating sink still
needs the graph to fire; confirm the executor module drives correctly with no
output layer.

title: dune-config: sub-detector abstraction (APA for HD, CRP for VD) in the noise-model body
description:
Generalize the noise-model config so the SAME body works across the (FD/PD) x
(VD/HD) matrix where the sub-detector unit differs: APA for HD, CRP for VD.  The
detector schema already abstracts these as the "anodes" array; ensure the
noise-model body and NoiseModeler grouping refer to the sub-detector purely
through the schema (ident/name/faces/adc), with no HD/APA- or VD/CRP-specific
hardcoding.  Confirm both PDHD (APA) and PDVD (CRP) detectors resolve through the
noise-model body identically.  Depends on the schema params task.

title: dune-config: WCT noise-model job body (Undigitizer -> NoiseModeler), single sub-detector
description:
Add a new WCT job body under wct/job/ (e.g. noise-model.jsonnet) plus any needed
parts, composing a single-sub-detector graph:

  frame input (DAQ-decoded ADC) -> Undigitizer -> NoiseModeler (sink)

driven by the detector schema (parts(detector, anode_index, ...)).  Reuse the
lib/graph.jsonnet + lib/ends.jsonnet conventions.  Configure:
  * Undigitizer from the anode's {anode, resolution, gain, fullscale, baselines}.
  * NoiseModeler with {dft, isnoise=NoiseRanker (ITraceRanker), threshold, groups
    from the detector's noise_groups, nfft, outname}.

This body TERMINATES in a sink (NoiseModeler), unlike sim/sigproc which end in a
FrameBoundarySink.  Its side effect is the noise-spectra JSON at `outname`.
Depends on the schema params task (undigitize gain + noise_groups).

title: dune-config: detector-schema undigitize (gain) + per-sub-detector noise-group params
description:
Extend the dune-config detector schema (wct/lib/schema.jsonnet) and the PDHD/PDVD
detector descriptions with the parameters the noise-model body needs but the
sim/sigproc schema does not yet carry:

  * Undigitize/electronics: an anode `gain` (linear electronics gain) alongside
    the existing adc{resolution,baselines,fullscale}.  Undigitizer requires
    {anode, resolution, gain, fullscale, baselines}; today adc{} lacks gain
    (Digitizer's gain lives in the sim body, not the detector description).
  * NoiseModeler grouping: a per-sub-detector `noise_groups` description — either
    an explicit [{groupID, channels}] list, a path to a groups JSON, or null
    (single group).  Decide whether groups are derived from the channel map
    (ddm-3j8.1.13) or authored per detector.

Keep to STRUCTURE + structural defaults in schema.jsonnet (values stay in the
per-detector files), matching the existing schema conventions.  Add validate()
coverage for the new fields.

title: [epic] dune-config: DAQ noise-model job (Undigitizer + NoiseModeler) over raw DUNE DAQ HDF5, per sub-detector
description:
Produce a runnable DUNE noise-characterization job in devel/dune-config that
applies a WCT graph terminating in the NoiseModeler sink, fed from raw DUNE DAQ
HDF5 files read through the libraries already developed under the ddm-3j8.1
epic (dune-daq-hdf read, dune-daq-codec decode, dune-daq-wct bridge + channel
map).  The job's product is a SIDE EFFECT: per-channel-group average noise
half-spectra written to JSON by NoiseModeler at termination (no frame output).

WCT data flow (one sub-detector):
  DAQ-decoded IFrame (ADC) -> Undigitizer (ADC->voltage) -> NoiseModeler (sink).
  Undigitizer needs {anode, resolution, gain, fullscale, baselines}; NoiseModeler
  needs {dft, isnoise=ITraceRanker(NoiseRanker), threshold, groups, nfft, outname}.

Both config domains are delivered, kept strictly separate per the dune-config
architecture (ddm-4pz):
  * wct/   : a new noise-model job body + parts, driven by the detector schema.
  * phlex/ : a side-effect (sink-terminated) workflow variant that runs the WCT
             body over a daq-hdf source with NO downstream sink module.

FACTORING REQUIREMENT (core of this epic): the config must abstract the target
detector and its sub-detectors so the SAME job works for HD (sub-detector = APA)
and VD (sub-detector = CRP) designs.  The dune-config detector schema already
abstracts these as the per-detector "anodes" array; this epic generalizes that
into the noise-model body and NoiseModeler channel grouping, and adds the
electronics/undigitize parameters the schema does not yet carry.

COORDINATION REQUIREMENT (the "something extra"): a given input DAQ HDF5 file
contains only some sub-detectors (a set of SourceIDs/DetIDs / readout units),
which is generally a subset of the configured detector's full sub-detector set.
The job must reconcile the CONFIGURED sub-detector set against the sub-detectors
actually PRESENT in the input file and build/fan the noise-model graph over the
intersection (per-sub-detector NoiseModeler instances or grouped output).  This
touches the channel map (ddm-3j8.1.13/.16) and multi-anode assembly (ddm-4pz.7).

Reference: WCT Undigitizer (devel/wire-cell-toolkit/sigproc, IFrameFilter) and
NoiseModeler (IFrameSink) — docs under devel/wire-cell-toolkit/docs/components/.

Depends on the DAQ read-path work being usable at the Phlex level (ddm-3j8.1.6,
gated on Phlex 0.3.0 source/driver) and on real-fragment channel-map validation
(ddm-3j8.1.16) for a physically-correct end-to-end result.

title: HDF5 address scheme v2: 4-level product subpath (stage/plugin/algorithm/suffix) + root-attribute scheme stamp
description:
Replace the 2-component product tail (creator='plugin:algorithm' percent-escaped
to %3A + suffix) with a fixed 4-level subpath per the 2026-08-03 design
discussion (Brett ratified Option A):

  <cell layer/number pairs>/<stage>/<plugin>/<algorithm>/<suffix>/<payload...>

- Fixed arity 4 makes the product/payload boundary deterministic (variable
  depth rejected as ambiguous vs payload subtrees).
- stage: phlex 0.3 product_selector/store field; unset normalized to the
  reserved default 'CURRENT' (registration_api.hpp defaults output_product
  stage to "CURRENT"_id).  Captures a field the old scheme silently dropped.
- plugin/algorithm: from product_specification accessors (module label / node
  name) -- NOT product_selector::to_string() (lossy + format-unstable).
- suffix: empty optional -> '_'.
- layer NOT repeated (already the innermost cell pair).
- Root attribute stamps the convention (e.g. phlex.address.scheme =
  'stage-plugin-algorithm-suffix/v1') per the Arrow schema-versioning policy,
  so scanners/readers parse by declared convention (cf ddm-c3s.15).
- No compatibility with previously written files (test artifacts only).
Touches: phlex-arrow-common (StoreAddress build + parse inverse), phlex-arrow-hdf
(read-address config handling, output stamp, integration-test expectations).
arrow-hdf stays agnostic (escaping retained as safety net; colons no longer
occur in practice).
notes:
=== IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-03, Claude) ===
arrow-hdf 6a1d8ed: Hdf5File::write_root_attr/read_root_attr (generic file-root
string attrs; arrow-hdf stays convention-agnostic).
phlex-arrow-common dd7279e: StructuredAddress = cells + stage/plugin/algorithm/
product; make_address emits the FIXED 4-component tail (stage ''->CURRENT,
other empties->'_'); parse_address consumes it; store_structured uses
algorithm_name::plugin()/algorithm() accessors (stage normalized to CURRENT --
phlex 0.3.2 store does not expose stage publicly; revisit when it does);
read-side config keeps the single 'plugin:algorithm' creator string via new
split_creator/canonical_creator helpers; CellHierarchy ProductLoc keeps the
canonical form (stage not yet represented in the hierarchy).  Constants
kAddressSchemeAttr='phlex.address.scheme', kAddressScheme=
'stage-plugin-algorithm-suffix/v1', kCurrentStage, kEmptyPart.
phlex-arrow-hdf 838cbd4: output stamps the scheme at file create; input gates
on it (mismatch throws, absent = legacy best-effort); ArrowHdfSource
canonicalizes the configured writer creator before matching scan results.
BONUS FIX: the three integration workflows still referenced pre-rename wcp_*
wire-cell-phlex modules and had been silently failing to load plugins;
repaired to wcph_frame_gen/wcph_frame_observer.

VERIFIED: phlex-arrow-common ctest 5/5; phlex-arrow-hdf ctest 6/6 (incl. the
write->scan->read round trip through the new scheme); full-chain smoke
unchanged (566772 traces) with the new layout
/event/0/CURRENT/<plugin>/<algorithm>/<suffix>/... , ZERO %3A escapes, and
h5dump shows phlex.address.scheme='stage-plugin-algorithm-suffix/v1' at root.
Old files are NOT readable by new builds (test artifacts only, per decision).
close_reason: 4-level stage/plugin/algorithm/suffix product subpath + root-attribute scheme stamp implemented across arrow-hdf/phlex-arrow-common/phlex-arrow-hdf; all suites green (5/5, 6/6), full chain re-verified with the new %3A-free layout; stale wcp_* integration workflows repaired en route.

title: Interim work-around: edep-sim-usable E-field/aux conventions for dunecore PDVD/PDHD GDML
description:
Until the GeGeDe dual-target epic lands, provide a temporary way for edep-sim
to see the drift E-field (and clean aux conventions) in the dunecore
PDVD/PDHD geometries.  Without it the field is silently zero and
EDepSimDokeBirksSaturation degrades to SecondaryDeposit==EnergyDeposit ->
n_electrons~0 (the ddm-496 mechanism), leaving the sampler 'quanta' mode and
the ddm-69y.8 quanta-vs-recombination cross-check gated.

Candidate work-arounds (pick in-issue):
- xerosere-owned GDML overlay/sed step producing edep-sim variants with
  auxtype="EField" VECTOR values (needs per-detector drift direction:
  PDHD horizontal +-x, PDVD vertical) and SegmentDetector auxtype.
- OR teach devel/edep-sim to accept the LArSoft "Efield" scalar given a
  configured drift axis (less clean; upstream-ambiguous).
The recombination-mode sampler default keeps the full chain unblocked either
way; this work-around only restores the quanta path / edep-sim's own
light-charge partition.
notes:
2026-08-05 GDML E-field verdict (for the upstream edep-sim issue): NOT a GDML non-compliance -- a consumer-convention mismatch. GDML has NO field concept; the only field carrier is the generic <auxiliary> extension (AuxiliaryType, gdml_core.xsd:196-201: auxtype/auxvalue unconstrained xs:string, auxunit optional). No field/Efield element exists anywhere in the schema. Both files are schema-valid.
Mismatch (edep-sim EDepSimUserDetectorConstruction.cc): (1) CASE - dunecore writes auxtype='Efield', edep-sim matches exactly 'EField'/'ArbEField' (:335), case-sensitive -> aux skipped -> zero field. (2) SHAPE - dunecore auxvalue='500*V/cm' scalar; edep-sim ParseEField (:128) needs vector '(x,y,z) V/cm' and drops no direction. (3) edep-sim ignores auxunit, parses unit from value string (ParseUnit :114, the PR#98 routine).
Compliant fix we can emit: <auxiliary auxtype='EField' auxvalue='(-500,0,0) V/cm'/> per drift axis -- edep-sim's own convention, no LArG4-ism needed. Upstream asks: document EField aux + optionally accept LArSoft spelling (case-insensitive + scalar+direction).

title: Upstream edep-sim fix: ParseUnit accepts LArSoft '0.5*cm' auxiliary values
description:
